rule: Heat-treated tooling parts without case hardening: use QPQ; case-hardened locating pins: black oxide or IZBP with masked functional area
note: masking is MF-06; the process choice is a design-intent judgement

rule: Auxiliary (reference) dimensions are shown in parentheses and carry no tolerance.
note: same rule as DM-010. ISO 129's term for a reference dimension is 'auxiliary dimension'; triage.py already cites §3.1 for DM-010. 'No tolerance applies' also means the general tolerance (IS 2102) does not apply to it.
quote: An auxiliary dimension is given in parentheses and no tolerance applies to it.

rule: Every auxiliary (bracketed) dimension can be derived from other dimensions on the drawing or in a referenced document; a bracketed value that nothing else produces leaves that size or location undefined for production.
note: adds detail to CN-004. CN-004 checks that a reference dimension agrees with what it summarises; this adds that a derivation must exist at all. Reuse the chain arithmetic; if no chain yields the bracketed value, warn (it may come from a related document).
quote: It does not govern production or inspection operations and is derived from other values shown on the drawing or in related documents.

rule: All dimensional information needed to define the part completely (size and location of every feature) is on the drawing.
note: same rule as MX-001. DM-01 is merged into MX-001 (size) and MX-002 (location); triage.py already cites ISO 129 §3.2.1 for MX-01/02/03.
quote: All dimensional information necessary to define a part or component clearly and completely shall be shown directly on a drawing unless this information is specified in associated documentation.

rule: Where dimensional information is not shown on the drawing, the drawing names the associated document that specifies it.
note: adds detail to MX-030. MX-030 flags dimensions deferred to the model. ISO allows deferral only to associated documentation, so accept a deferral note that names a document (the PARI pattern 'TORQUE AS PER STD-DES-01-00') and flag an unnamed one ('SEE 3D MODEL'). Whether a 3D model counts as associated documentation is PARI's call (DM-16).
quote: shall be shown directly on a drawing unless this information is specified in associated documentation.

rule: Each feature is dimensioned only once on the drawing; the same dimension is not repeated in another view.
note: same rule as DM-002. triage.py already cites §3.2.2 for DM-02.
quote: Each feature shall be dimensioned once only on a drawing.

rule: No more dimensions are shown than are needed, and no feature is defined by more than one dimension in any one direction; an extra closing dimension is allowed only as a bracketed auxiliary dimension.
note: same rule as DM-003. Exception b) ('where the addition of an auxiliary dimension would be advantageous') is the bracket exception DM-003 already has.
quote: No feature of a part or an end product shall be defined by more than one dimension in any one direction.

rule: A feature may carry an additional dimension when it gives the size at an intermediate production stage (e.g. before carburizing and finishing); the duplicate and conflicting-value checks must allow such stage sizes.
note: adds detail to DM-002. An exception for DM-002 and CN-002 (two values on one feature). To recognise a stage size the checker needs a label (BEFORE CARBURIZING / BEFORE GRINDING / BEFORE PLATING); ISO does not prescribe the wording, so the label list is an assumption. Links to MF-005 (heat treatment stage).
quote: where it is necessary to give additional dimensions at intermediate stages of production (for example, the size of a feature prior to carburizing and finishing)

rule: Dimensions are placed on the view or section that shows the feature most clearly.
note: same rule as MX-10. DM-08 is merged into MX-10 (deferred). A vision-LLM pass could approximate it, but the existing disposition is deferred.
quote: Dimensions shall be placed on the view or section that most clearly shows the corresponding features.

rule: All dimensions on a drawing use the same length unit (mm for PARI); no dimension is given in inches, cm or m, and there is no dual dimensioning.
note: adds detail to TB-009. TB-009 checks that units are stated; this checks every dimension value for a foreign unit suffix or bracketed dual value. Probe of 60 PARI samples: no inch dimensions, but the template SURFACE AREA field shows in^2 on all 60 (not a dimension; ask PARI). ISO 129's figures use a decimal comma (25 ±0,06) and PARI uses a point; the preview text sets no rule on this.
quote: Each drawing shall use the same unit (for example, millimetres) for all dimensions

rule: Dimension values do not carry the unit symbol; the drawing's unit may instead be stated once in a note.
note: adds detail to TB-009. Conflicts with PARI practice: 19 of 60 sampled drawings put 'mm' in Solid Edge hole callouts ('Ø 6.00 mm THRU', "C'BORE Ø 15.00 mm") and some notes ('CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2mm'). It would fire on about a third of drawings, so PARI must decide whether ISO 129 applies strictly. TB-009's units note is the 'note' ISO allows.
quote: for all dimensions but without showing the unit symbol. In order to avoid misinterpretation, the predominant unit symbol on a drawing may be specified in a note.

rule: Values in units other than the drawing's length unit (e.g. torque in N·m, pressure in kPa) show their unit symbol with the value.
source_document: ISO 129:1985 Technical drawings, Dimensioning, general principles (preview edition, clauses 1 to 4.4.2)
note: Scan notes for numbers next to torque/pressure/force/load keywords that have no unit. PARI torque notes point to a standard ('TORQUE AS PER STD-DES-01-00'), so this mainly catches typed values. Title-block SURFACE AREA in in^2 has its symbol (ISO is met) but is imperial on a metric drawing. Hardness units are covered by MF-010.
quote: (for example, N·m for torque or kPa for pressure), the appropriate unit symbol shall be shown with the value.

rule: Functional dimensions (fits, mating sizes, distances between functional features) are dimensioned directly, not left to be derived from other dimensions.
source_document: ISO 129:1985 Technical drawings, Dimensioning, general principles (preview edition, clauses 1 to 4.4.2)
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70L, book 134)
note: LLM warning only: the model must guess which dimensions are functional (toleranced or fit-coded sizes, shoulders, bearing seats). Related to DM-04 / MD-11 (dimension from functional datums, phase2_3d), but not the same rule.
quote: Functional dimensions should be shown directly on the drawing wherever possible (see figure 2).

rule: Where a functional dimension is given indirectly, the tolerances of the dimensions that produce it are tightened so the derived value still meets the functional tolerance.
note: adds detail to TL-12. Figure 3: functional 25 ±0.06 is kept by showing 40 ±0.05 and 15 ±0.01 (tolerances add to 0.06). The arithmetic is code, but the functional tolerance comes from design intent or the assembly, hence phase2_3d.
quote: Occasionally indirect functional dimensioning is justified or necessary. In such cases, care shall be exercised so that the effect of directly shown functional dimensioning is maintained.

rule: Notes do not prescribe a production process or inspection method unless it is essential to function or interchangeability.
note: same rule as NM-12. NM-12 is 'deferred' in the mapping; an LLM pass over the note text could raise info-level warnings, so v1 is proposed. PARI's own guidelines require some processes (heat treatment, welding process, NDT); those count as essential and must not fire.
quote: Production processes or inspection methods should not be specified unless they are essential to ensure satisfactory functioning or interchangeability.

rule: Non-functional dimensions are arranged in the way that is most convenient for production and inspection.
note: Needs knowledge of the machining set-up and measuring practice (like MC-11, deferred).
quote: The non-functional dimensions should be placed in a way which is most convenient for production and inspection.

rule: Projection (extension), dimension and leader lines are thin continuous lines.
note: adds detail to LY-01. Line width and dash pattern are in the PDF vectors, but line-type classification is deferred with LY-01. The Solid Edge dimension style makes violations rare.
quote: Projection lines, dimension lines and leader lines are drawn as thin continuous lines as shown in ISO 128

rule: Projection lines extend slightly beyond their dimension line.
note: No numeric overshoot is given in ISO 129. Set by the CAD dimension style; low value.
quote: Projection lines shall extend slightly beyond the respective dimension line (see figures 4 and 5).

rule: Projection lines are perpendicular to the feature being dimensioned; where they have to be oblique, they are parallel to each other.
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70L, book 134)
note: Vector geometry check on paired projection lines; deferred as drafting quality.
quote: Projection lines should be drawn perpendicular to the feature being dimensioned. Where necessary, however, they may be drawn obliquely, but parallel to each other (see figure 6).

rule: Where a dimension goes to the intersection of construction or projection lines (a theoretical corner), those lines extend slightly beyond their intersection point.
note: adds detail to MX-24. Figure 7 shows a dimension to the meeting point of an inclined face and a flat face. MP-10 / DM-13 cover dimensioning to virtual sharps; this adds how the construction lines are drawn.
quote: Intersecting construction and projection lines shall extend slightly beyond their point of intersection (see figure 7).

rule: Projection and dimension lines do not cross other lines unless this is unavoidable; where they must cross, neither line is broken.
note: adds detail to VW-06. Counting crossings between dimension-line vectors is feasible, but 'unavoidable' needs judgement. Figure 10 shows nesting shorter dimensions inside longer ones to avoid crossings.
quote: In general, projection lines and dimension lines should not cross other lines unless this is unavoidable ... neither line shall be shown with a break

rule: Where a feature is drawn with a break, its dimension line is shown unbroken across the break (method 2 drawings interrupt it only to insert the value).
note: adds detail to VW-13. VW-13 (broken views show true length) is phase2_3d; this part is a 2D geometry check on the dimension line.
quote: A dimension line shall be shown unbroken where the feature to which it refers is shown broken (see figure 9), except as indicated in 4.4.1, method 2.

rule: A centreline or a part outline is never used as a dimension line (it may stand in for a projection line).
note: adds detail to CN-003. CN-003 matches each value to a dimension line; this adds that the matched line must be a dedicated thin dimension line. Needs line-type classification (LY-01, deferred). Projection-line checks must accept centrelines and outlines.
quote: A centreline or the outline of a part shall not be used as a dimension line but may be used in place of a projection line

rule: Every dimension line ends in a distinct termination (arrowhead or oblique stroke) or, for running dimensions, starts at an origin indication.
source_document: ISO 129:1985 Technical drawings, Dimensioning, general principles (preview edition, clauses 1 to 4.4.2)
note: Arrowheads are in the v1 vector layer. Allow one termination on radius dimensions (4.3.5) and on partly drawn dimension lines of half-shown features (figure 23), and dots in tight spaces (4.3.3).
quote: Dimension lines shall show distinct terminations (i.e., either arrowheads or oblique strokes), or, where applicable, an origin indication.

rule: Terminations have the standard form, sized in proportion to the drawing: arrowhead barbs at an included angle of 15° to 90° (open, closed or filled), oblique strokes at 45°, and the origin indication as an open circle of about 3 mm diameter.
note: adds detail to LY-03. Measurable from vectors but set by the CAD dimension style (LY-03); low value per drawing. 4.3.2: terminations no larger than needed to read the drawing.
quote: the arrowhead, drawn as short lines forming barbs at any convenient included angle between 15° and 90°.

rule: One arrowhead style (open, closed or filled) is used throughout a drawing; an oblique stroke or a dot replaces an arrowhead only where space is too small.
source_document: ISO 129:1985 Technical drawings, Dimensioning, general principles (preview edition, clauses 1 to 4.4.2)
supporting_reference: related rule LY-04; Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70L, book 134)
note: A 'pick one and be consistent' check: tell filled from open arrowheads by the vector path's fill attribute; accept strokes or dots only on short dimension lines (figure 24). LY-04 covers style consistency across sheets (phase2_3d).
quote: One style of arrowhead termination only shall be used on a single drawing. ... where space is too small for an arrowhead, the oblique stroke or a dot may be substituted

rule: Arrowheads sit inside the limits of the dimension line where there is room; they go outside, on an extended dimension line, only where space is limited.
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70L, book 134)
note: 'Where space is available' needs a threshold (dimension line length versus arrow length plus text); not given by ISO 129.
quote: Arrowhead terminations shall be shown within the limits of the dimension line where space is available (see figure 13).

rule: A radius dimension has exactly one arrowhead, with its point on the arc end of the dimension line (inside or outside the outline).
source_document: ISO 129:1985 Technical drawings, Dimensioning, general principles (preview edition, clauses 1 to 4.4.2)
note: Find radius values by the 'R' prefix in the text layer and count arrowheads on the matched dimension line. Our inference, not ISO's: an 'R' value with two arrowheads across the centre may be a diameter tagged as a radius, which is worth a warning.
quote: Only one arrowhead termination, with its point on the arc end of the dimension line, shall be used where a radius is dimensioned (see figure 15).

rule: Dimension values are large enough to stay legible on the original drawing and on reproductions.
note: same rule as LY-02. ISO 129 gives no minimum height; that comes from ISO 3098-1 and ISO 6428 (referenced). The text layer gives character height, so this could become v1 once a minimum is agreed.
quote: Dimensional values shall be shown on drawings in characters of sufficient size to ensure complete legibility on the original drawing as well as on reproductions made from microfilms.

rule: No line crosses or splits a dimension value.
source_document: ISO 129:1985 Technical drawings, Dimensioning, general principles (preview edition, clauses 1 to 4.4.2)
supporting_reference: related rule VW-06; Westermann Tables Sections and sectional views (pdf 69L, book 132)
note: Intersect each value's text box with vector lines other than its own dimension line. Hatching and centrelines through values are the usual cases; a line through a digit can cause a misread.
quote: They shall be placed in such a way that they are not crossed or separated by any other line on the drawing.

rule: A drawing places dimension values by one method throughout, ISO 129 method 1 (aligned with the dimension line, read from the bottom or right) or method 2 (all read from the bottom), and orients angular values to suit that method.
source_document: ISO 129:1985 Technical drawings, Dimensioning, general principles (preview edition, clauses 1 to 4.4.2)
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70R, book 135); ISO 129:1985 4.4.1 method 2 (p9); ISO 129:1985 4.4.1 methods 1 and 2 (p9)
note: Text-layer rotation, corrected for the page /Rotate (PARI pages are rotated 90°): method 1 has vertical values turned 90° CCW, method 2 has all values at 0°. Exclude values on leaders (4.4.2 c), which are horizontal in both methods. In 60 PARI samples all used method 1. Neutral on ISO vs ASME (method 2 resembles ASME unidirectional).
quote: Values shall be indicated on a drawing according to one of the following two methods. Only one method should be used on any one drawing.

rule: With method 1, values are parallel to their dimension lines and read from the bottom or the right-hand side of the sheet, never from the top or left; values on oblique lines follow figure 17.
source_document: ISO 129:1985 Technical drawings, Dimensioning, general principles (preview edition, clauses 1 to 4.4.2)
note: On the displayed sheet, the text direction must lie in (-90°, +90°]. Upside-down or top-to-bottom text fails. In 60 PARI samples, no numeric text read from the top or left.
quote: However, values shall be indicated so that they can be read from the bottom or from the right-hand side of the drawing.

rule: With method 1, values sit near the middle of the dimension line, above it and clear of it.
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70L, book 134)
note: Exceptions: superimposed running dimensions (5.2.2, not in this preview) and the 4.4.2 placements (near a termination, on an extension, on a leader).
quote: Dimensional values shall be placed parallel to their dimension lines and preferably near the middle, above and clear of the dimension line (see figure 16).

rule: With method 2, all values read from the bottom of the sheet, and non-horizontal dimension lines are broken, preferably near the middle, to take the value.
note: Only fires on method 2 drawings; none of the 60 PARI samples used method 2.
quote: Dimensional values shall be indicated so that they can be read from the bottom of the drawing sheet. Non-horizontal dimension lines are interrupted

rule: Angular values are oriented to suit the method in use: with method 1, aligned with the arc (figure 18) or horizontal (figure 19); with method 2, horizontal only (figure 19 or 22).
note: It only bites on method 2 drawings (a non-horizontal angular value fails). Pairs with the one-method rule.
quote: Angular dimensional values may be oriented either as in figure 18 or figure 19. ... either as in figure 19 or figure 22.

rule: A dimension value may sit off-centre near one termination (partly drawn dimension lines), above an extension of the dimension line beyond a termination, or at the end of a leader that touches a short dimension line. Matching values to dimension lines must accept these placements.
note: adds detail to CN-003. An implementation exception that prevents false positives in CN-003 and the method-1 placement checks. Figure 23 also shows partly drawn diameter dimension lines with one arrowhead (half-shown features).
quote: The positioning of dimensional values frequently needs adapting to different situations. ... at the end of a leader line which terminates on a dimension line that is too short

rule: On a multisheet drawing, sheet 1 carries the complete title block, the revision block and the general notes.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: PARI's template may repeat the full title block on every sheet; the check is only that sheet 1 is complete and holds the general notes and revision history.
quote: The first sheet of a multisheet drawing shall always contain the complete Title block, List of Material, Revision Block, and general notes.

rule: All sheets of a multisheet drawing are the same sheet size.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: Page size from the PDF page box, with a small tolerance for export differences. Related to TB-015 (correct template and sheet size).
quote: All sheets of multisheet drawings shall be of the same letter size.

rule: Only sheet 1 states the total number of sheets ("SHEET 1 OF n"); continuation sheets show only their own number.
note: adds detail to TB-010. GSFC / MIL-STD-100 convention. PARI's "Sheet x of y" on every sheet is fine and should not be flagged; listed only as a source variant for TB-010.
quote: Numbering of continuation sheets shall be limited to stating the specific sheet number (e.g., "SHEET 2," "SHEET 3") without specifying the total number of sheets.

rule: A zone grid is present on multisheet drawings of D size (about A1) and larger, and on single-sheet drawings of E size (about A0) and larger.
note: adds detail to LY-09. Inch sheet sizes; LY-09 uses A2 and larger. Zone letters and numbers are border text, so this can move to v1 together with LY-09.
quote: Zoning is mandatory for multisheet drawings "D" size and larger and single-sheet drawings "E" size and larger.

rule: Every continuation sheet repeats the title-block identification (drawing number, sheet number, title and scale), and its drawing number and title match sheet 1.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: NASA's list also has the organisation (CAGE) code and the name and date fields, which PARI's template doesn't repeat on every sheet as far as we know.
quote: The Title block of continuation sheets for multisheet drawings shall contain information listed in items 1, 2, and 4 through 11.

rule: When a note or title-block option applies "where indicated" or to "surfaces marked", the matching marker symbol or flag appears at least once on the field of the drawing.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: Generalises WPM-003 (hardened area shown) and RQ-003 to any "where indicated" note; 2.4.4.5 (p31) has "MASK ALL SURFACES MARKED". Needs marker detection in vectors; text proxy: the symbol or flag id cited in the note appears elsewhere on the sheet.
quote: TEST HARDNESS PER ASTM E-18 WHERE INDICATED ON FIELD OF DRAWING THUS

rule: Metric general tolerances are set by number of decimal places: whole mm ±1, one decimal ±0.5, two decimals ±0.25, angles ±1°, radii and chamfers ±0.5.
note: adds detail to TB-008. Conflicts with PARI's IS 2102 general tolerances (by size range and class, not by decimals). With a decimal-keyed block, each untoleranced dimension's decimal count must exist in the block. 10.2.1i (p101) lets the values be adjusted per design. Quote read from the Fig. 2b image.
quote: 2 DECIMAL ±0.25 1 DECIMAL ±0.5 DECIMAL ±1 ANGLE ±1° RAD/CHAM ±0.5

rule: A general edge-break note is present: remove all burrs and sharp edges, R 0.25 or chamfer maximum.
note: adds detail to NM-001. Gives NM-001's deburr note a value. Presence is v1; the value (0.25 mm here) is PARI's to set. Quote read from the Fig. 2b image (the text layer scrambles this figure).
quote: REMOVE ALL BURRS AND SHARP EDGES R 0.25 OR CHAMFER MAX

rule: A default surface roughness (Ra 3.2 µm in the GSFC metric format) is stated for surfaces without their own symbol.
note: same rule as TL-016. Default value is GSFC's; PARI's may differ. Quote read from the Fig. 2b image.
quote: 3.2 FINISH IN MICRO- METERS

rule: Unit weight is entered in the title block when required.
note: same rule as TB-014.
quote: WT: Enter unit weight calculated at time of design if required.

rule: Designer and drafter printed names and their dates are entered in the title block.
note: same rule as TB-005.
quote: DESIGNER: Enter designer's printed name and initials.

rule: The checker named in the title block is a different person from the designer and the drafter.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: PARI leaves Checked/Approved blank at submission (TB-016), so this only applies once the field is filled, e.g. when a released drawing is re-reviewed.
quote: This name shall be an independent name from all other names on the drawing.

rule: Each approver's name in the title block is tagged with their function (ENG, STRESS, QA, MATL, ELEC).
note: GSFC approval procedure; PARI's template defines its own approval fields.
quote: For example, after each approval name, note the following: "ENG" for engineer, "STRESS" for stress engineer, "QA" for quality assurance engineer

rule: The Next Assembly and Used On fields name the drawing on which the part is next used and the program.
note: adds detail to TB-11. Only if PARI's template FR-DES-006-01 has such fields and the WP requires them.
quote: NEXT ASSY: Enter drawing number on which the part is next utilized, modified, or assembled.

rule: Where the drawing has an NDE required / not required option, exactly one is marked, and an NDE-required entry cites the method code or a note.
note: adds detail to WF-014. Same pattern as WPW-001 (one option chosen in welding notes). Checkbox state may be vector-only; text proxy is the code or "see note" reference.
quote: The appropriate "Non-Destructive Examination (NDE) Required" block shall be checked off, and the addition of the applicable code or "see note XX" shall be added where required.

rule: A part with a hardness requirement states whether hardness testing is required and where: location optional, or at locations marked on the field.
note: adds detail to MF-010. GSFC's title block makes this compulsory for every part; for PARI, limit it to parts that carry a hardness value. GSFC's test method is ASTM E-18 (Rockwell).
quote: The appropriate Hardness Testing block shall be checked off regardless of whether the part is flight hardware or not.

rule: CAD-produced drawings carry a block recording the software, version and file name.
note: GSFC CAD-file rule.
quote: On CAD-produced drawings, add a 3.5-inch-long by 0.88-inch-high block

rule: The drawing states its unit system: dimensions in millimetres, or the metric / hybrid metric-inch box marked.
note: same rule as TB-009. Also the model note "DIMENSIONS ARE IN MILLIMETERS" (2.4.4.1, p28) and Fig. 2b "UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED DIMENSION ARE IN MM".
quote: METRIC/HYBRID METRIC-INCH: Add "X" to type of drawing block.

rule: The material callout gives the material specification and grade plus the final condition or temper (e.g. 6061-T6, 303 COND A).
note: adds detail to MF-01. Adds "final condition" to MF-01. Needs a per-material list of which conditions are mandatory (aluminium temper, steel heat-treat condition); PARI's material table (WPM rules) could hold it.
quote: MATERIAL SPEC.: Enter the applicable material specifications, number, and final condition.

rule: Each revision entry records the revision symbol, a description, the date and the approval, plus the zone when the drawing is zoned.
note: adds detail to RV-001. Fig. 31a (p81): zone column not required on C size and smaller.
quote: REVISIONS - ZONE: Enter zone (where used).

rule: Paints, adhesives and protective coatings are specified in note form rather than as list-of-material items.
note: PARI uses a Finish/Treatment title-block field (TB-013); whether a note is also wanted is PARI's call.
quote: Paint, adhesives, and protective coatings shall appear in note form.

rule: The drawing title starts with the basic noun, followed by modifiers separated by commas (e.g. "BRACKET, MOUNTING").
note: adds detail to TB-003. ASME Y14.100 / MIL noun-first convention. PARI titles may use natural word order.
quote: A modifier is separated from the noun or noun phrase by a comma and from any preceding modifier by a comma.

rule: The noun in the title is not abbreviated, and no part of the title is in parentheses.
note: adds detail to TB-003. 2.1e: "Parentheses are not used to enclose any portion of the drawing title." The abbreviation part needs the approved list (LY-11).
quote: The noun, or noun phrase, is never abbreviated.

rule: Program or project names go in the Used On field, not in the title (except on the top assembly).
note: adds detail to TB-003. Depends on PARI's template having a Used On / project field (TB-11).
quote: Program names (or abbreviations) should be added to the "Used On" block and not the Title block

rule: Each word is abbreviated the same way throughout the drawing (one form for singular, plural and tenses), and word-combination abbreviations are not split.
note: adds detail to LY-11. Flags mixed forms on one drawing (e.g. THK / THK. / THICK, DIA / Ø). The approved list itself stays needs_pari (LY-11). 2.2d: abbreviations never at the expense of clarity.
quote: The same abbreviation shall be used for all tenses, the possessive case and the singular and plural forms of a given word.

rule: Notes do not contradict a specification they invoke, unless the note is an intended, stated deviation from it.
note: adds detail to NM-002. Notes take precedence over specifications, so an unintended conflict silently overrides the spec. The LLM needs some knowledge of the cited standard.
quote: notes conflicting with referenced specifications shall not be placed on a drawing unless they are necessary for deviations from certain provisions of the specification.

rule: Each sheet carries the security classification of its own content, with the warning note above the title block.
note: adds detail to TB-018. US national-security marking; PARI's ownership / confidentiality note is TB-018.
quote: Each sheet of a multisheet drawing shall be individually classified as to its contents.

rule: General notes sit in the preferred area (upper left, or left of the revision block), and nothing is placed in the space below the revision block kept for future revisions.
note: Fig. 22b note (p60): no information beneath the revision block. PARI's template fixes the notes area, so low value.
quote: This location should be avoided whenever practical because the space required for revisions cannot be anticipated.

rule: General notes are numbered consecutively from 1, with no gaps or repeated numbers.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: On bilingual A1/A2 sheets, check the English and French lists separately and that they match in count.
quote: General notes are numbered consecutively downward.

rule: Every note reference on the drawing field ('SEE NOTE 5' or a flag number) points to a note that exists, and every note marked as a flag note is flagged at least once on the field.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
supporting_reference: related rule NM-07; HNF-64101 3.11.16 (p29)
note: RQ-003 is the heat-treatment case of this rule; the verifier (A3) merges duplicate findings.
quote: Note numbers may be identified on the field of the drawing by placing the note number in a pennant-shaped flag

rule: The general notes are headed "UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED" (or "EXCEPT AS NOTED").
note: No PARI client drawing uses this heading: it would fire on 1,174 of 1,175 sheets. On bilingual sheets accept the French equivalent heading.
quote: Use either of the following statements as main heading for notes: "Except as noted" or "Unless otherwise specified."

rule: No note contains an unfilled template blank or placeholder (e.g. "XXX", "____", "(insert ...)", "TBD"); template notes that do not apply are removed.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: On PARI sheets 'XXXXXX' is also left in fields such as 'HEAT TREATMANT PROCESS:XXXXXX' (an unfilled placeholder: 23 client sheets have a run of X), while a run of X drawn along a surface marks the area to be hardened (WPM-003). The check must tell them apart, e.g. by whether the run follows a field label.
quote: Significant information is to be inserted where blank(s) are indicated and, for most cases, the notations in parentheses are for information only.

rule: When a part is plated, coated or stress-relieved, a note states whether dimensions (and roughness values) apply before or after that process.
note: adds detail to WPS-004. Model notes also: "ALL DIMENSIONS APPLY AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT", "DIMENSIONS TO APPLY AFTER STRESS RELIEF", and hard chrome "DIMENSIONS SHOWN APPLY AFTER PLATING" (p30). A concrete text check behind WPS-004 / MF-08.
quote: DIMENSIONAL LIMITS AND SURFACE ROUGHNESS DESIGNATIONS APPLY (state "BEFORE" or "AFTER") PLATING.

rule: The drawing states the dimensioning and tolerancing standard it is to be interpreted to.
note: same rule as LY-06. GSFC's title block carries "DRAWING INTERPRETED PER GSFC-X673-64-1". ISO vs ASME is still open with PARI.
quote: DIMENSIONING AND TOLERANCING TO BE INTERPRETED IN ACCORDANCE WITH ANSI Y14.5M-1982.

rule: Gear drawings state the gear accuracy (quality) grade and the standard it refers to.
note: adds detail to MX-018. Metric equivalent is an ISO 1328 grade. 10.3b-c (p104) list AGMA 2000-A-88 and 390.03A.
quote: GEAR TOLERANCES TO BE IN ACCORDANCE WITH AGMA STANDARD QUALITY (insert number).

rule: A heat-treatment note names the process specification and the resulting hardness with its scale (Rockwell, Brinell or Vickers).
note: adds detail to MF-010. Adds "names the process specification" to MF-010's value-and-scale check.
quote: HEAT TREAT IN ACCORDANCE WITH MIL-H-6875 TO XXX. (XXX = "Rockwell," "Brinell," or Vickers").

rule: A welded or brazed part in heat-treatable aluminium states the heat treatment and final temper required after joining (e.g. solution treat and age to T6).
note: adds detail to WF-004. Given as a model note; the reviewer judges whether the loss of temper at the weld matters. PARI fabrications are mostly steel, so rare.
quote: AFTER WELDING, SOLUTION HEAT TREAT AND ARTIFICIALLY AGE TO T-6 CONDITION PER MIL-H-6088.

rule: The welding note names the welding specification, process, class and filler metal.
note: adds detail to WF-007. Adds process and filler metal to WF-007. ISO equivalents: process number per ISO 4063, quality level per ISO 5817, filler classification per the consumable standard. PARI's welding guideline may already fix the filler (7018 / 8018).
quote: FUSION WELD IN ACCORDANCE WITH MIL-STD-2219, PROCESS ___ CLASS ___ USING FILLER METAL ___ AND APPROPRIATE FLUX.

rule: Weld joint design and dimensions are specified on the drawing.
note: same rule as WF-008.
quote: (Joint dimension and design should be specified on the drawing.)

rule: Brazing and soldering notes name the specification, the type or grade, and the filler (braze or solder) material.
note: adds detail to WF-007. Rare at PARI; same pattern as the welding note.
quote: SILVER SOLDER IN ACCORDANCE WITH MIL-B-7883, TYPE ___ GRADE ___ USING SOLDER MATERIAL QQ-B-654, CLASS ___.

rule: Each plating or coating callout names its specification and the attributes that specification needs: type and class, colour for anodising and paint, thickness for hard chrome.
note: adds detail to TB-013. PARI's process list (WPS-001) should supply the attributes per process (e.g. zinc plating thickness and passivation).
quote: HARD CHROME PLATE (size)—(size) THICK PER QQ-C-320, TYPE ___, CLASS ___; DIMENSIONS SHOWN APPLY AFTER PLATING.

rule: Plating is not used on space-flight hardware in areas sensitive to flaking (optics, electronics).
note: Space-flight specific.
quote: Plating notes are generally not for space flight hardware use in restricted areas such as optics, electronics, etc., due to flaking.

rule: Paint colour is specified by a colour-standard number.
note: same rule as MF-013. FED-STD-595 in the book; RAL at PARI.
quote: COLOR ___ IN ACCORDANCE WITH FED-STD-595 (color number).

rule: The coating suits the base material: anodise or chromate conversion on aluminium, passivation on stainless steel, phosphate on iron and steel, anodic treatment per AMS 2488 on titanium.
note: adds detail to WPS-002. The book groups its coating notes by base material; use them as seed pairs for WPS-002's table, not as a closed list.
quote: Note for CRES: PASSIVATE PER QQ-P-35, TYPE ___.

rule: Surfaces to be masked during a finishing process are marked on the drawing and called out in a note.
note: same rule as MF-006.
quote: BEFORE ELECTROPOLISHING, MASK ALL SURFACES MARKED

rule: Each NDT note names the method, the inspection standard and the type/class or acceptance level.
note: adds detail to WF-014. Also "RADIOGRAPHIC INSPECTION OF ALL WELDS IN ACCORDANCE WITH MIL-STD-00453" and penetrant per a code. PARI's PRD-GD-DES-11 lists MPI / UT / DPT.
quote: ULTRASONIC INSPECTION PER MIL-STD-2154, TYPE ___ (Insert "I" or "II"), CLASS ___.

rule: When an inspection must happen before finish machining (e.g. etch and penetrant), a separate note says so.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: Context is GSFC fracture-critical parts; generalises to any inspection tied to a manufacturing stage.
quote: If areas of a part are to be etched and inspected prior to finish machining, a separate drawing note should call out this requirement to avoid costly mistakes.

rule: Leak-tight parts state the maximum leak rate, the test medium, the instrument sensitivity and the pressure differential.
note: adds detail to SC-05. Vacuum / pressure parts, outside the v1 families.
quote: THIS PART SHALL HAVE A LEAK RATE OF NOT MORE THAN (1 x 10-7 CC/SEC OF HELIUM) WHEN MEASURED BY A CALIBRATED MASS SPECTROMETER

rule: Threaded inserts are cleaned, baked out and dry-film lubricated before installation.
note: Spacecraft contamination control.
quote: CLEAN THREADED INSERTS WITH TRICHLOROETHANE AND BAKE OUT AT 100 DEGREES CELSIUS FOR 3 TO 4 HOURS PRIOR TO INSTALLATION.

rule: Threaded-insert callouts name the insert type and the installation standard.
note: adds detail to MX-029. Metric shops usually cite the insert maker's part number or the wire-insert standard.
quote: INSTALL THREADED INSERTS PER XXX. (XXX = "MS33537" for coil type, "MS51835" for Keen type, or "MIL-I-45932/1" for thin wall type.)

rule: On a coated part with threaded inserts, the notes give the order: holes tapped before coating, inserts installed after coating.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: Model note; the LLM judges whether the sequence is clear.
quote: TAP ALL HOLES PRIOR TO COATING; INSTALL THREADED INSERT AFTER COATING.

rule: A part-marking note gives the method (stamp, etch, engrave or ink), the character height, the depth for stamped or engraved marks, and the content and location ("as shown").
note: adds detail to NM-09. Also the rubber-stamp note: ink or paint per a named specification. NM-09 (whether marking is needed) stays needs_pari; this checks completeness once marking is called for. The depth value is inch.
quote: STEEL STAMP, ETCH, OR ENGRAVE (size) HIGH CHARACTER AS SHOWN, X .010 +.005 -.000 DEEP.

rule: Where a material certificate is required, a note says so and names the item it applies to.
note: same rule as NM-10.
quote: A MANUFACTURER'S CERTIFICATION OF MATERIAL SPECIFICATION COMPLIANCE MUST BE SUPPLIED WITH PART

rule: Packaging and identification of the delivered part (bag and tag with the part number) is stated where needed.
note: same rule as NM-11.
quote: BAG PART PER MIL-P-116, METHOD ___, AND TAG WITH PART NUMBER.

rule: A general roughness note gives the value for machined surfaces and says whether unmachined stock surfaces stay as supplied (rolled, extruded, drawn), or states "finish all over".
note: adds detail to TL-016. Relevant to PARI plates and bars machined on some faces only. Related model notes: "FINISH (symbol) ALL OVER", "ALTERED SURFACES TO HAVE (symbol)".
quote: SURFACE ROUGHNESS AS XXX: MACHINED SURFACES . (where XXX is "ROLLED," "EXTRUDED," or "DRAWN").

rule: A general note sets the maximum radius for unspecified inside corners.
note: same rule as NM-001.
quote: INSIDE CORNERS R ___ MAXIMUM.

rule: Weldments that need it carry a note to straighten and stress-relieve after welding.
note: same rule as WF-004.
quote: UNIT TO BE STRAIGHTENED AND STRESS-RELIEVED AFTER WELDING.

rule: A local note (hole, thread or other feature callout) states how many features it covers, unless a leader goes to each feature.
note: adds detail to MX-003. Adds the explicit exception (a leader to each feature) to DM-06's quantity element. Needs a count of identical features in the view (vector circles) against the nX prefix.
quote: Each note shall state the number of features to which it applies unless a leader is drawn to each feature.

rule: Every dimension is controlled by the general tolerance unless it is marked MAX, MIN, REF, BASIC or as a datum, carries its own tolerance, or is controlled by a note or invoked document.
note: adds detail to MX-012. Gives MX-012 its exemption list. A single-limit value not marked MAX/MIN falls under the general tolerance.
quote: general tolerances entered in the supplementary portion of the Title block shall control all dimensions applied to the drawing, except those specifically labeled "Max," "Min," "Ref," "Datum," or "Basic,"

rule: Specifications are cited by basic document number unless a particular issue is intended, and cancelled or superseded specifications are not cited.
note: adds detail to NM-03. Citing an issue or date freezes that issue for procurement. 2.4.4 (p28): check the specification has not been cancelled or superseded. Needs PARI's list of current standards (NM-03).
quote: Normally, only the basic document number of a specification should be shown on the drawing

rule: Views, dimensions and notes stay inside the drawing border and do not run into the margins.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: Vector and text bounding boxes against the border-frame rectangle, excluding zone labels and template items printed in the margin.
quote: Views, dimensions, etc., shall not extend into the margins of the drawing.

rule: Only the views needed to define the part are drawn; one or two views are fine when notes or dimensions complete the definition, and pictorial views are only auxiliary.
note: same rule as VW-01. Kept with VW-01's disposition.
quote: only those views shall be drawn that are necessary to convey the required characteristics of the part.

rule: Mechanical drawings use third-angle orthographic projection.
note: adds detail to TB-07. PARI's projection angle is still open; GSFC's title block carries the third-angle symbol.
quote: Third-angle orthographic projection shall be used for mechanical engineering drawings.

rule: Lines use two widths, thick and thin, in about a 2:1 ratio, with the standard line types (visible, hidden, centre, phantom, section, cutting plane).
note: same rule as LY-01. ISO 128-20 uses the same 2:1 ratio.
quote: Two widths of lines, i.e., thin and thick, with their widths in the proportions of 1:2, shall be used.

rule: Dimension lines end in arrowheads at both ends; leaders end in an arrowhead on a line or a dot inside the part outline.
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70L, book 134)
note: Vector-geometry check; low value on Solid Edge output.
quote: Arrowheads should always terminate at a line; dots should be within the outline of an object.

rule: All lettering on the drawing is upper case.
note: ASME/MIL convention (also 2.2a); ISO 3098 allows lower case. PARI's English + French notes may be mixed case.
quote: All lettering shall be uppercase (capital letters).

rule: Text reads horizontally from the bottom of the sheet (unidirectional); where that is not practicable, it reads from the right-hand side.
note: ASME unidirectional practice; ISO 129-1 also allows aligned dimensions. PARI's convention unconfirmed.
quote: placed in a horizontal reading position as far as practicable.

rule: Lettering heights follow the table: drawing number and title 0.25 in, dimensions and notes 0.16 in, list-of-material and name blocks 0.14 in.
note: adds detail to LY-02. Inch heights (0.16 in is about 4 mm). Use PARI / ISO 3098 heights for LY-02 instead.
quote: Dimensions, tolerances, limits, notes, subtitles, tables, revision, and zone letters on the field of the drawing .16

rule: Text is not compressed to fit ("fit text" is not allowed).
note: The PDF text matrix exposes horizontal scaling, so this could become a cheap v1 check.
quote: Note: Use of fit text is not allowed.

rule: The drawing scale is one of the preferred scales: 1/1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/10, 1/20, 2/1, 4/1, 10/1, 20/1.
note: adds detail to TB-006. Differs from ISO 5455 (1:2, 1:5, 1:10, 1:20 ... 2:1, 5:1, 10:1). Needs PARI's list.
quote: The scales preferred for engineering drawings are full size 1/1, reduced 1/2, 1/4, 1/10, 1/20, and enlarged 2/1, 4/1, 10/1, 20/1.

rule: The title-block scale field holds a ratio (or NONE for unscaled diagrams) without the word SIZE; "& NOTED" is added when some views use other scales.
note: adds detail to TB-006. PARI uses ISO ratio form (1:2); accept either separator.
quote: The scale, as noted above, or the word "NONE" must be entered in the Title block. Do not use the word "SIZE" following the ratio.

rule: Any view drawn at a scale other than the title-block scale carries its own scale label (e.g. "DETAIL A SCALE 4/1").
note: adds detail to VW-008. Check by comparing measured vector lengths with dimension values per view. The book says not to label views drawn at the title-block scale; PARI may label every detail view (VW-008), so don't flag extra labels.
quote: The scale of the view shall be stated only when it differs from that noted in the Title block, which represents the majority of views and sections.

rule: A dimension whose value does not match the drawn geometry at the view scale is marked not-to-scale (underlined, or NTS).
note: Catches overridden values (DM-09) without the 3D model: measured length x view scale vs the value. ISO 129-1 uses the same underline. The book's 0.03 in figure is for pencil drawings only, so the mismatch threshold is the team's to set. 9.3.2 (p96): computer-generated drawings must be to scale.
quote: it is required to indicate that a particular feature is not to scale by underlining the dimensions with a straight line.

rule: CAD drawing geometry is entered at full (1:1) scale.
note: CAD-file rule.
quote: The geometry of CAD-produced drawings shall be entered into the electronic database at one-to-one (full) scale.

rule: Turned parts are usually drawn with the larger diameters to the left.
note: adds detail to VW-11. "Usually", so info only. The vision summary can report the orientation.
quote: Lathe-turned parts are usually drawn with the larger diameters to the left.

rule: A section is taken through an exterior view, not through another section.
note: Vision may be able to answer this; kept with the other view-layout checks.
quote: A sectional view shall be made through an outside view and not through another sectional view.

rule: Each section is located by a cutting-plane line with reference letters and arrowheads showing the viewing direction, and each removed view is lettered where shown and at its origin.
note: same rule as VW-003.
quote: The location of a section is indicated by a cutting plane with reference letters and arrowheads showing the direction in which the section is viewed.

rule: A rotated view, section or detail states the angle and direction of rotation.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: The text check covers labels that say ROTATED; spotting an unlabelled rotated view needs vision or geometry. 3.5.4: details should not be rotated at all.
quote: If views have to be rotated, the angle and direction of rotation must be given.

rule: Shafts, bolts, nuts and similar parts lying in the cutting plane are not hatched, and one general hatch pattern is used whatever the material.
note: same rule as VW-09. 3.5.2g (p47): the cast-iron (general-purpose) hatch is used for all materials.
quote: Shafts, bolts, nuts, etc., which are in a cutting plane should not be cross-hatched.

rule: A section or view shown away from its cutting plane (another zone or sheet) carries the zone and sheet of its origin, and the cutting plane carries the zone and sheet where the view is shown.
note: adds detail to VW-003. 3.5.6 (p50) shows the format: "SEE VIEW A-A / 5A / SH3" at the origin and "1D / SH1" under the view.
quote: When sections are remotely located, zone information shall be added to both locations (i.e., from where the section is taken and to the location where the section is shown).

rule: A section or view is not placed directly in front of the cutting-plane or viewing-plane arrows (it lies behind the plane, third-angle style).
note: adds detail to VW-02. Depends on the projection convention.
quote: Views located directly ahead of viewing plane arrowheads are absolutely prohibited.

rule: Section, view and detail letters are unique on the drawing, and I, O, Q and X are not used.
note: adds detail to VW-003. Same idea as MD-008 (datum letters) and RV-007 (revision letters). Uniqueness is generic; the excluded set is ASME practice, so keep it configurable.
quote: The letters "I," "O," "Q," and "X," either as a single letter or as double-letter entries, shall not be used.

rule: Section, view and detail letters are assigned alphabetically: sections as hyphenated pairs (A-A), details as single letters, continuing AA, AB after Z.
note: adds detail to VW-003. Gaps can be legitimate after revisions (a released letter is not reused), so info only.
quote: Identifying letters for sections, views, and details are assigned in alphabetical sequence

rule: An altered or selected vendor part drawing names the vendor part number, vendor name and address, defines the alteration, re-identifies the part, and is labelled as such above the title block.
note: Drawing type outside v1 (modified bought-out parts). The same goes for modification, source-control and specification-control drawings (4.11, 4.13, 4.14).
quote: it shall specify the part to be altered or selected by vendor number, name, and address and shall completely delineate the alteration or selection.

rule: A detail drawing states the material and every finish, protective coating and process needed to make the finished part.
note: same rule as TB-013. 3.1 (p37): complete drawings contain or reference all data for fabrication and any test requirements. Also overlaps TB-012.
quote: A detail drawing shows all the information necessary for fabricating an item, including the material from which it is made and those finishes, protective coatings, and processes required

rule: A detail drawing shows one part only (no multi-detail drawings).
note: GSFC wants one drawing number per part for estimating and configuration tracking (also App. A (e)); ASME Y14.24 allows multi-detail drawings.
quote: Only one item (detail part) shall be presented per drawing.

rule: A weldment is defined on one drawing that dimensions each piece and the finished assembly; pieces are not detailed on separate drawings unless they need extensive machining.
note: adds detail to WF-10. App. A (b) (p119): keeps overall tolerancing with one manufacturer. Depends on how PARI structures fabrication drawings.
quote: In the case of weldments, the parts shall not be individually detailed on separate drawings (due to the consumable material allowances that would have to be shown on detail drawings)

rule: A matched-set drawing states the mating characteristics, serial-marks each part of the set, and carries "Maintain and furnish only as a matched set".
note: Assembly-type drawing. 2.4.4.8 also has "MAINTAIN AS MATCHED SET AFTER MACHINING".
quote: The parts shall be uniquely marked with a serial number identification to indicate a matched set.

rule: Before a part is detailed, a government or industry standard part is considered; a drawing is made only when no standard part fits.
note: adds detail to BM-16. For single parts that look like catalogue items (dowels, spacers, washers, keys): warning only.
quote: If neither of these contain a part satisfactory for the design needs, a drawing shall be prepared.

rule: Dimensions controlled by a tool or template are flagged to a tooling note and shown as reference.
note: adds detail to DM-010. Only if PARI makes parts to drilling templates or fixtures.
quote: When affected by tooling, dimensions and their tolerances shall be flagged on the engineering drawing to the above note and enclosed in parentheses to indicate reference information only.

rule: Composite-material drawings define the ply count, stacking sequence, ply angles, prepreg materials, a coordinate reference and a ply table.
quote: The drawing shall specify the multi-ply laminate configuration that defines the number of plies, the stacking sequence, the ply angle orientation, the prepreg fiber-resin materials

rule: Drawing numbers follow the GSFC format (G + size letter + seven digits), and sketch (SK) numbers are not used on manufacturing drawings.
note: adds detail to TB-001. GSFC numbering.
quote: Drawing numbers shall consist of assigned basic seven-digit numbers, prefixed by the letter "G" (signifying GSFC) and a second letter signifying the drawing size

rule: The part number of a non-standard part is, or includes, the drawing number.
note: adds detail to TB-001. Depends on PARI's numbering (drawing number vs part number fields).
quote: Each nonstandard item shall be identified by a part number that shall be, or shall include, the drawing number.

rule: Mirror-image (shown and opposite) parts on one drawing carry separate part numbers, with the drawn part identified as "shown".
note: adds detail to MX-021. The -1/-2 odd/even scheme is GSFC's; the general point is that both hands are identified.
quote: Symmetrically opposite parts shall be designated by -1 (shown) and -2 (opposite) carrying the odd/even relationship to higher numbers as necessary.

rule: On a tabulated drawing, every variant has a dash number and a value for every tabulated characteristic; the base number alone does not identify a part.
note: Only if PARI makes tabulated (family) drawings.
quote: The basic drawing number alone shall not be used to identify a part.

rule: Where the same item is defined by several documents, they are cited in GSFC's order of precedence (federal and military first, company standards last).
note: US-government procurement rule.
quote: When identical parts or assemblies of equal quality are identified by more than one document, the item shall be referenced on drawings in the following order

rule: Revision letters run alphabetically without I, O, Q, S, X or Z; after Y come AA, AB, and after AY come BA, BB.
note: adds detail to RV-007. RV-007 excludes I, O, Q; the extra S, X, Z is ASME Y14.35 practice. Parts and index lists (8.2.3, p84) exclude I, O, Q, X instead.
quote: letters I, O, Q, S, X, and Z shall not be used as revision symbols. Following letter Y, use AA, AB, etc.; after AY, use BA, BB, etc.

rule: All sheets of a multisheet drawing carry the same revision level, raised on every sheet even when that sheet did not change.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: ASME Y14.35 also allows sheet-by-sheet revision levels; switch off if PARI uses that. Complements TB-004 (single sheet).
quote: Level of revision shall be changed on each drawing sheet whether or not that particular sheet is affected.

rule: The revision history of a multisheet drawing is recorded on sheet 1, and the other sheets refer to it ("See sheet 1 for revisions").
note: adds detail to RV-001. PARI's template may repeat the revision table on every sheet.
quote: The revision description block on all sheets other than sheet 1 shall state "See sheet 1 for revisions."

rule: Each revision marker on the field (revision symbol at the point of change) matches an entry in the revision block, and each directly incorporated revision has at least one marker.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
supporting_reference: related rule RV-02; NAAMS Section A Sec. 18.3; Sec. 18.6 (p4)
note: RV-02 (were all changes marked?) needs the previous revision; this cross-reference needs only the current PDF. PARI may use triangles rather than circles. Changes made through a change order need no field markers (7.4).
quote: A symbol (e.g., "A3") enclosed in a circle shall appear in the field of drawing at the point of revision.

rule: When changes are made through a change order, the revision entry cites the change-order number.
note: same rule as RV-003.
quote: the Revision Block must state "See EO number ___ for changes" or "See Revision Notice number ___" in the revision description column.

rule: Each revision entry is dated and initialled by the person incorporating the change, the checker and the responsible engineer.
note: same rule as RV-001. The number of approvers is PARI's choice.
quote: the person incorporating the revision, the person assigned to check the incorporation, and the cognizant engineer responsible for the revision all shall date and initial the revision block

rule: Revision descriptions say what changed, giving the previous value where a value changed ("WAS ... / NOW ..." or "REMOVED / ADDED").
note: adds detail to RV-001. 6.2 item 9 (p77): describe the change with "Was" and "Now" or "Remove" and "Add".
quote: (1) R.188 WAS R.250 (2) ADDED .500, 1.500 AND 2.000 DIMS (3) REM'D .750 AND 7.000 DIMS

rule: A redrawn drawing records "Replaces revision X with/without change", drops earlier revision entries and keeps the original names and dates.
note: GSFC release procedure.
quote: When a drawing is redrawn without changes, the phrase "Replaces Revision (old revision letter) Without Change" shall be added to revision block

rule: On a weldment drawing, pieces with different material specifications or tempers are each identified by an item number linked to their material.
note: adds detail to BM-01. BM-01 is other_family (assemblies); weldments are in v1 scope, so this is the weldment form of it.
quote: The item number system of identification shall also be used to locate pieces on drawings of inseparable assemblies when material specifications or material tempers differ from one another.

rule: Assembly drawings carry a list of material giving item number, quantity, part number, description, material and material specification, with no skipped item numbers.
note: adds detail to BM-01. 1.4 item 18 (p20): do not skip item numbers on new drawings.
quote: to provide the individual part or subassembly item number, quantity required, part number, description, material, and material specification.

rule: Dimensions follow the part's relationship to its mating parts, not insignificant theoretical centre lines.
note: same rule as MD-11. Needs mating-part knowledge. App. A (a): centre-line chains force the machinist and inspector into arithmetic.
quote: Dimensions shall be chosen and placed on drawings based on the parts interrelationships with mating parts, not to insignificant theoretical center lines.

rule: Primary, secondary and tertiary datum features are lettered in alphabetical order (A primary, B secondary, C tertiary).
note: Alphabetical datum order is an ASME habit; ISO 5459 sets no order. Depends on PARI's ISO vs ASME choice. Check the main datum reference frame order in feature control frames; frames that legitimately use another order (e.g. |B|A|) exist, hence info.
quote: Primary, secondary, and tertiary datum features shall be labeled in alphabetical order when creating a new drawing.

rule: Reference dimensions are kept to a minimum.
note: adds detail to DM-010. App. A (n) (p120): too many reference dimensions make checking, inspection and cost estimating harder. No numeric limit in the book; a count per view could feed the LLM.
quote: Use a minimum of reference dimensions on drawings.

rule: Position tolerances (basic-dimensioned features) reference datum letters; implied datums are not allowed.
note: same rule as MD-003.
quote: Implied datums (when no datum letter(s) are specified) are no longer acceptable.

rule: Angles use one format throughout (decimal degrees or degrees-minutes-seconds), and an angle's tolerance uses the same format as its value.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
supporting_reference: D&T tutorial slides Unit of measure; Tolerancing - Plus/Minus (p7, 8, 56)
note: Flags mixed angle formats or radians on one drawing.
quote: angles stated in degrees, minutes, and seconds, or in degrees and decimal of a degree (preferred), shall be used when dimensioning parts.

rule: The number of decimal places in a dimension equals that of its tolerance.
note: same rule as LY-005. Metric practice; LY-005 already encodes it.
quote: The number of decimal places in the dimension shall be the same as the number of places in the required tolerance.

rule: Surface-roughness values are given in micrometres and taken from the preferred series 0.025-50 µm (N1-N12).
note: adds detail to TL-016. Same series as ISO 1302. A non-series value (e.g. Ra 2.5) or a microinch value gets flagged.
quote: Surface texture values shall be noted in micrometers (µm).

rule: Forces are in newtons, stresses in megapascals, pressures in kilopascals and masses in kilograms; no imperial units appear in notes or the title block.
note: 10.2.1e-g (p99-100): stresses in MPa, pressure in kPa, mass in kg. PARI may use bar or MPa for pressure; the core check is no imperial units on a metric drawing (US material names under WPE-001 excepted).
quote: Forces, such as tensile and shear loads, shall be shown in newtons (N).

rule: Metric threads use the preferred diameter/pitch combinations (M1x0.25 ... M8x1, M10x1.25, M12x1.25 ... M39x2).
note: adds detail to MC-005. Aerospace (ISO/TC20) series with fine pitch from M8 up. General industry uses ISO 261/262 coarse (M8x1.25, M10x1.5, M12x1.75). Do not use for PARI without confirmation: it would flag every coarse thread.
quote: Preferred diameter/pitch combinations for threaded fasteners are shown in the following table, in accordance with ISO/TC20/SC4 Resolutions 169 and 220.

rule: Fits use the preferred metric limits-and-fits designations (ANSI B4.2, equivalent to ISO 286).
note: same rule as TL-013.
quote: Preferred Metric Limits & Fits (ANSI B4.2-1978) encompasses tolerance required designations, preferred limits, basic sizes, and symbols.

rule: Untoleranced metric dimensions are governed by a named general-tolerance standard.
note: same rule as TB-008. IS 2102 at PARI.
quote: General Tolerances for Metric Dimensioned Products (ANSI B4.3-1978) is used for metric dimensions without tolerance designations.

rule: On dual-dimensioned drawings, converted values are rounded to the precision the total tolerance calls for, and converted limits stay inside the original limits.
note: Only relevant if PARI shows inch equivalents for US customers (cf. WPE-001). Rounding table in 10.2.2.2c (p103); inside rounding (10.2.2.2d): upper limit rounded down, lower limit rounded up.
quote: When converted, tolerances must never exceed the originally specified limits

rule: Surface texture is specified to ANSI B46.1 and its symbols drawn to ANSI Y14.36.
note: ISO 1302 / ISO 21920-1 symbols differ in detail; depends on PARI's ISO/ASME choice.
quote: Symbols depicting acceptable surface conditions shall be in accordance with ANSI Y14.36-1978 (R 1987) (or later revisions).

rule: Thread callouts follow the thread standard's designation (e.g. M profile per ANSI B1.13M) and representation (ANSI Y14.6).
note: same rule as MX-004. ISO 965-1 / ISO 6410 equivalents for PARI. The book's examples carry the thread class (4-40 UNC-2A, .438-20 UNF-3B).
quote: Screw-thread conventions, methods of specifying, and design shall be in accordance with the following specifications

rule: Weld symbols and their arrow-side / other-side meaning follow ANSI/AWS A2.4.
note: same rule as WF-01. ISO 2553 and AWS A2.4 differ on arrow / other side (ISO 2553 system A uses a dashed identification line); reading one as the other puts the weld on the wrong side. PARI must confirm which.
quote: Basic weld symbols and their location significance shall be in accordance with ANSI AWS A 2.4-86 (or later revisions).

rule: Dimensioning to mating surfaces avoids tolerance build-up between them.
note: same rule as TL-12.
quote: Dimensioning shall be to primary or mating surfaces. Unwanted buildup of tolerances between mating surfaces should be avoided.

rule: Coordinate (ordinate) dimensions run left to right and bottom to top from the origin, so all values are positive (first quadrant), or start from functional datums.
note: adds detail to MP-012. "Whenever possible", so info only. Flags negative ordinate values or an origin away from the lower-left datum corner.
quote: Whenever possible, dimensions should be left to right and bottom to top (Quadrant I, all positive numbers) or from datums established by design requirements.

rule: A datum is assigned to a physical surface or a feature of size, not to a centre line.
note: same rule as MD-06. Kept with MD-06's disposition.
quote: A datum should always be assigned to a physical surface or a feature of size.

rule: Hole patterns are preferably located with position tolerances on basic dimensions rather than ± coordinate tolerances.
note: PARI locates holes with ± tolerances under IS 2102, so a preference for position tolerancing would fire on most sheets. A preference, not a requirement: info only. PARI may routinely use ± location under IS 2102.
quote: it is preferred that hole patterns be true positioned, regardless of use, since tolerancing specified in the true position block is the controlling factor.

rule: Basic-dimensioned hole patterns are not also given ± location tolerances; positional and plus/minus methods are not mixed.
note: same rule as MX-011.
quote: The combined usage of positional tolerancing with plus and minus methods as related to basic dimensioned patterns is discontinued and replaced with the composite tolerancing method.

rule: Materials are chosen for low outgassing (space-flight hardware).
note: adds detail to MF-12. Space-specific (NASA RP-1124 data, 10.7 p107); comparable to MF-12's WP-specific material requirements.
quote: Specify low-outgassing materials.

rule: The marking method does not create stress raisers on highly stressed parts: steel stamping, engraving and etching are avoided there in favour of ink marking.
note: adds detail to NM-09. The book's scope is flight hardware; generalise to fatigue-loaded or thin parts. Also: identical parts with different uses should be serialised.
quote: Do not steel stamp engrave, or etch on flight hardware to prevent material stress concentrations.

rule: Position tolerances on tapped holes, threaded inserts and slip-fit features are regardless of feature size (no MMC or LMC modifier).
note: TL-10 (MMC/LMC used deliberately) is deferred; this is a direct frame read for threaded features. Under ASME Y14.5M-1982 RFS needed an explicit symbol; in ISO and ASME Y14.5-2009+ it is the default.
quote: Positional tolerance should be specified as "Regardless of Feature Size" when applying to thread inserts, tapped hole locations, and slip fit designs.

rule: Tolerances are no tighter than the application needs.
note: same rule as TL-003. Also: true position tolerances can be as loose as the application allows.
quote: Loose tolerances make inspection easier and allow fewer rejected parts.

rule: Edge radii, inside corner radii and chamfers are specified.
note: same rule as NM-001. The NSTS 07700 crew-safety sizes are space-specific; the "specify them" part is general.
quote: Edge radii, in-plane corner radii, and protrusion chamfers must be specified to space flight standard size requirements.

rule: The bottom corners of counterbores carry a radius, so there is no sharp internal corner.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: May be covered by a general inside-corner note (NM-001); the LLM judges whether it is.
quote: Specify radii at the bottom of counterbores to prevent sharp corners, which could develop into stress cracks, particularly on flight parts.

rule: For press fits, the interference range is stated next to the item callout.
note: adds detail to TL-002. Assembly-drawing callout; on PARI detail drawings the fit code or limits (TL-002, TL-013) cover it.
quote: Only the amount ".000X to .000X interference" should be stated next to the item call out.

rule: Position tolerances on tapped holes, threaded inserts and dowel-pin holes use a projected tolerance zone with its height.
source_document: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center GSFC-X-673-64-1F Engineering Drawing Standards Manual (1994)
note: Only where a position tolerance is used. Needs the projected-zone (P) symbol from the symbol font. ISO 1101 has the same modifier.
quote: Add a projected tolerance zone dimension to the true position tolerance when specifying threaded inserts, tapped holes, or dowel pins.

rule: Fastener torque requirements are stated by specification or a torque table flagged to the callouts.
note: same rule as BM-07.
quote: fastener size and torque requirements can be tabulated in the General Notes and flagged to item call-outs in the field of the drawing.

rule: A bolted joint does not pair countersunk holes in one part with tapped holes in the mating part (double fixation), and matched drilling is avoided.
note: Needs the mating part. On a single drawing, a countersunk pattern could at most raise a reminder.
quote: A pattern of countersunk holes in one part and tapped holes in the mating part leaves no tolerancing for either part, resulting in bending stresses in the screw.

rule: Stainless-to-stainless threaded joints have an anti-galling measure (bronze insert, dry-film lubricant or coated fasteners).
note: Needs the mating fastener material.
quote: To avoid severe galling in CRES-to-CRES fastener applications, consider the following possibilities

rule: Split and toothed lock washers, and silver-plated hardware near electronics, are avoided.
note: Aerospace contamination rules.
quote: These types of washers are not used on aerospace flight projects for several reasons; the worst is possible particulate contamination.

rule: The part is designed to be machined in as few set-ups as possible.
note: same rule as MC-11.
quote: Design a part so it can be made with the least amount of machine setups possible.

rule: A revision of an existing drawing is checked against the standard and title-block format it was created under; only new drawings must use the current format.
note: adds detail to TB-015. Exception to TB-015 (latest template): stops false flags on old drawings being revised. §3.12 (p29) adds that released drawings need not be reformatted (title block, revision block, parts list). Needs PARI's policy on legacy drawings and a way to tell new from revised (revision > initial).
quote: Revisions to previously released drawings shall comply with the standards under which they were created.

rule: Drawings are delivered as AutoCAD DWG files with bound X-references and NCS V6 layer names.
note: Hanford CAD-file handling (also layer naming in Appendix A, pp. 38-70, and the CTB pen table, Table 2 p11). PARI uses Solid Edge and v1 sees only the PDF.
quote: Drawings developed on CAD programs other than AutoCAD shall be converted to the standard AutoCAD program “DWG” format prior to releasing the data files to DMCS.

rule: Line widths follow a scheme by usage: thin (0.25 mm) for dimension, extension, leader, hidden and centre lines; medium (0.35 mm) for visible object lines; wide (0.50 mm) for cutting-plane lines and borders.
note: adds detail to LY-01. Hanford/NCS multi-discipline values with a 1.4:1 visible-to-thin ratio; ISO 128 line groups use 2:1 (0.5/0.25 or 0.7/0.35), so PARI's template governs. Stroke widths are in the PDF vectors, but classifying each line by usage needs geometry analysis beyond v1.
quote: Dimension lines, leaders, extension lines, break lines, hidden objects, dotted lines, dashed lines, setback lines, center lines

rule: All sheets of a multi-sheet drawing are the same sheet size.
note: adds detail to TB-015. Sheet size comes from the PDF page box. Confirm PARI never mixes A1/A2 sheets within one drawing.
quote: All drawing sheets of a multiple sheet drawing are to be the same size.

rule: A metric drawing uses SI units only: no inch-pound values or units (inch marks, fractions, in, lb, lbf, psi), except declared dual dimensions and native inch trade designations (e.g. G 1/2 pipe threads).
source_document: HNF-64101 Rev 00 Preparation Standards for Engineering Drawings (Hanford, US DOE, 2020)
note: HNF states it for a drawing set; applied per drawing here. Exempt inch thread and pipe designations (1/4-20 UNC, G 1/2, NPT) and dual dimensions declared by a note. PARI's template prints its SURFACE AREA field in in^2 (1,160 of 1,175 client sheets, e.g. '15.54 in^2'), so that field is left out until PARI says whether it is intended; Capstone I flagged it on a PARI sample drawing as a unit conflict.
quote: Avoid mixing metric system and inch-pound system on drawing sheets on the same set of drawings

rule: Sheet sizes ANSI E, ISO A0 and roll or elongated sizes are not used.
note: Hanford site restriction. PARI's allowed sizes come from its own template (TB-015).
quote: Do not use ANSI "E" size, ISO "A0" size, and roll or elongated size drawings.

rule: A drawing that alters a purchased item states 'ALTERED FROM' with the manufacturer's part number, shows unaltered features only for orientation (their dimensions in parentheses), and fully dimensions and tolerances the alteration.
note: Applies only if PARI makes modification drawings of bought-out parts. Unaltered features in thin lines, the alteration in medium lines; a new part number is assigned. The parenthesised orientation dimensions behave like reference dimensions (DM-010).
quote: "ALTERED FROM (manufacturer's part number)" is placed in the Description column.

rule: Any acronym that is not a common industry abbreviation (e.g. a site-, customer- or project-specific term) is spelled out in a legend or general note on the drawing.
note: adds detail to LY-11. LLM picks out unfamiliar acronyms in the notes and looks for a definition; warning only. Industry abbreviations such as DIA and REF need no definition.
quote: Hanford site-specific acronyms are clearly defined by spelling out the acronym in the LEGEND or by using a general note.

rule: Abbreviations are used only where space does not allow the word, and only industry-accepted ones (e.g. DIA, SCH, REF).
note: same rule as LY-11. Lookup table: PARI's approved abbreviation list, or ASME Y14.38 if PARI follows ASME. 'Only when space does not permit' is judgement.
quote: Abbreviations on a drawing are used only when space does not permit the word(s) to be spelled out

rule: Abbreviations carry no punctuation other than the slash and hyphen; a period is added only where the abbreviation could be read as a word (e.g. 'ADD.').
note: ASME Y14.38 convention. PARI drawings may write 'THK.' or 'NO.', and the French notes may follow other rules. Enforce only if PARI adopts it.
quote: Punctuation marks, except the slant (/) and the hyphen (-), are not used when abbreviations are used on drawings.

rule: Any non-standard symbol used on the drawing is defined in a legend on the drawing or a referenced legend drawing; SI unit symbols need no definition.
note: Written mainly for system and schematic drawings; on detail drawings it would catch custom symbols. Needs symbol recognition, which v1 vision cannot do reliably.
quote: Symbology used on new drawings that defines components is traceable to a LEGEND placed on the drawing or a separate legend drawing

rule: Drawing lettering is all upper case, except unit symbols and other symbols that are lower case by definition (e.g. mm, g).
note: ASME Y14.2 convention; ISO 3098 allows lower case, and PARI's bilingual English/French notes may be mixed case. A simple text-layer check once PARI confirms.
quote: For CAD-developed drawings, lettering is all upper case Gothic as defined in ANSI Y14.2M

rule: Lettering is at least 3 mm high; 2.5 mm is allowed only for revisions on crowded existing drawings, not on new drawings.
note: adds detail to LY-02. Text height can be read from the PDF text layer (font size), so this is v1-feasible once PARI picks the limit. HNF's 3 mm is stricter than the 2.5 mm ISO-style minimum quoted in LY-02 (which is deferred). Table 1 (p10) also pairs text heights with line widths.
quote: Letter height is a minimum of 3 mm (.12"), except where lower case letters or metric symbols are used (e.g., mm and g).

rule: In the title block, the drawing title is at least 6 mm high on A1 and larger sheets (3 mm on smaller sheets), and the drawing number is 6 to 8 mm high.
note: adds detail to LY-02. Drawing-number height from §3.11.5 (p24): 'The drawing number shall be 6 mm to 8 mm'. PARI's template fixes these heights, so the check mainly catches edited title blocks.
quote: Height of the lettering in the title is a minimum of 6 mm (.24") for ISO A1 and ANSI D and F size drawings.

rule: Only the standard drafting font(s) are used; no non-standard fonts.
note: same rule as LY-03. Font names are in the PDF text layer, so this becomes a v1 lookup once PARI names its template fonts (LY-03 is listed as phase2_3d).
quote: Nonstandard fonts (i.e., fonts not supplied by AutoCAD) are not to be used.

rule: Fabrication and assembly drawings specify the material of every part (on a single-part drawing, the material callout).
note: same rule as TB-012. Hanford puts the material in the parts/material list; PARI uses the title-block material field.
quote: A parts/material list shall be used on fabrication and assembly drawings, but not on project construction drawings as specified in Table 3.

rule: Individual pieces of a weldment or other inseparable assembly are normally not given separate part numbers.
note: Parts-list practice. Relevant to how PARI identifies weldment pieces (item numbers rather than part numbers).
quote: The individual pieces of weldments or other inseparable assemblies normally are not numbered separately.

rule: A change that makes an item no longer interchangeable gets a new part number, and part numbers are never reused for a different item.
note: same rule as RV-06. §3.10.8.8 (pp20-21) lists the triggers (performance, interchangeability, alteration) and says 'Part numbers shall not be reused' (also TB-17). Needs the previous revision and PDM.
quote: Non-interchangeable items shall be identified with separate and unique part numbers.

rule: Part numbers are the drawing number plus a dash number: -010, -020 for assemblies and -001, -002 for detail parts.
note: Hanford part numbering.
quote: The primary assembly is assigned the -010 dash number.

rule: Deleted parts-list items are struck through with a double line or replaced by 'DELETED' under a change notice, new items are added at the end, and item or part numbers are not reused.
note: Parts-list revision practice for assemblies.
quote: Remove a part or material item by placing a double line through the part or material item (e.g., CAD or manual drawings).

rule: Purchased items in the parts list carry the manufacturer's part number (or vendor-information number).
note: same rule as BM-04.
