quote: Purchased items shall be identified in the parts/materials list with the manufacturer’s part number or vendor information (VI) number as applicable.

rule: Parts-list quantities are given in customary trade units, with 'AR' (as required) where the quantity is unknown or can vary.
note: adds detail to BM-14.
quote: The letters AR (as required) shall be used where the quantity is not known or where the quantity could vary.

rule: Item names are written noun first, followed by modifiers (e.g. 'ASSEMBLY, GANTRY'), in standard industry language.
note: adds detail to TB-003. Stated for parts-list descriptions; ASME Y14.100 uses the same noun-modifier style for titles. The book's own Figure 2 mixes styles ('ASSEMBLY, GANTRY' vs 'STABILIZER ROD'). Confirm PARI's title style before enforcing.
quote: The name of the item shall be listed first with supplemental descriptive words following.

rule: A material or item description is complete enough to procure it, e.g. a material given with its specification (ASTM A36).
note: same rule as MF-01. Figure 2 example: STABILIZER ROD, ASTM A36. The acceptable material standards are PARI's list (MF-01).
quote: The description of an item shall be complete and provide specifications sufficient to procure the item.

rule: Standard or catalogue items that the parts list fully describes are not drawn in detail.
note: Assembly/BOM practice; the inverse of BM-06.
quote: If the item can be completely described in the parts/materials list, it shall not be delineated on the drawing.

rule: When a field's specification is too long and is put in a general note or separate specification, the field refers to that note or document (e.g. 'SEE NOTE 4').
note: adds detail to RQ-003. Stated for the parts-list description. Generalises RQ-003 (heat-treatment field) to the material and finish fields: if a note carries the material or finish spec, the field should point to it rather than be blank.
quote: the general note or separate specification shall be referenced in the description column of the parts list

rule: New drawings use the latest company title block (template).
note: same rule as TB-015. Same section: 'Only one title block is to exist in any data file' (a CAD-file rule; per PDF sheet it means one title block per sheet). See the legacy-format exemption candidate.
quote: New drawings and drawings being redrawn into CAD are required to use the latest available title block.

rule: The drawing title clearly identifies the subject matter.
note: same rule as TB-003.
quote: The title clearly identifies the subject matter.

rule: The drawing title is at most 60 characters including spaces, contains no project or building numbers (those go in their own field), and names the drawing type.
note: adds detail to TB-003. Hanford title structure (system / subsystem / component, drawing type on the last line). Length limit and 'no project numbers in the title' generalise if PARI's template has a separate WP/project field (TB-11).
quote: The total number of characters, including spaces, does not exceed 60.

rule: All sheets of a multi-sheet drawing carry the same title.
note: Repeated in §3.11.2 (p23) and §3.12.10 (p32). A different title on one sheet suggests a sheet from another drawing.
quote: All multi-sheet drawings sheets shall have the same title (i.e. when a new drawing title is used, a new drawing number and sheet sequence must be used).

rule: The title block carries Hanford building, index and H-series drawing numbers chosen by site area.
note: same rule as TB-001. Hanford numbering (HDNS, Table 4 prefixes H-1 to H-14). Published source for the TB-001 idea that the number follows the company scheme; the scheme itself does not apply.
quote: Drawing numbers are assigned in accordance with the Hanford Site area that the drawing will represent.

rule: Every place the drawing number appears on a sheet (the title block and any secondary location, e.g. outside the border) shows the same number.
note: adds detail to TB-001. Passes trivially if PARI's template has only one location. A mismatch suggests copying from another drawing.
quote: There are two locations for the drawing number, in the title block and outside the right border of the drawing in zone “B.”

rule: The approval fields carry the printed initials, surname, company and signature of the drafting checker, discipline engineer, engineering checker and design authority per the site release procedure.
note: Hanford approval workflow (MSC-PRO-ENG-709). Conflicts with PARI submission practice, where Checked and Approved are blank at submission (TB-016).
quote: The initials and surname of the individual who checked the drawing for compliance are placed in the "Drafting Approved" block.

rule: The revision level is the same in the title block, the auxiliary revision box (if the template has one) and the latest entry of the revision block.
note: adds detail to TB-004. Extends TB-004 to every location the revision appears (Figure 10, p32).
quote: The current revision number is noted in the Title Block, auxiliary block just outside the right side of the drawing border, and in the REVISION block.

rule: Released revisions are numbered 0, 1, 2... with 0 for the initial release, and pre-release issues use letters A, B, C...
note: adds detail to RV-007. Hanford scheme. RV-007 assumes letters for released revisions. The checker should validate whichever scheme PARI uses and that pre-release and released symbols are not mixed.
quote: Numeric revision numbers are used. [...] Zero (0) is normally used for the initial release.

rule: The scale field shows the predominant scale; if none predominates it says (AS) SHOWN and every view carries its own scale; it says NONE when the drawing is not to scale.
note: adds detail to TB-006. PARI/ISO wording is usually 'AS SHOWN'. With AS SHOWN, every view (not only detail views, VW-008) needs a scale label.
quote: Enter predominant scale of the drawing or if the predominant scale of the drawing cannot be determined, enter "SHOWN" and identify the scale under each graphic.

rule: View and sheet scales are standard ratios (e.g. 1:2, 2:1, 1:10); non-standard ratios such as 1:3 are flagged.
note: Book gives examples only; suggested lookup table is the ISO 5455 recommended scales (1:2, 1:5, 1:10 ... 2:1, 5:1, 10:1). HNF's architectural inch scales (1/4"=1'-0") are not applicable.
quote: The use of non-standard scales such as 1/3, 1.315=1 are discouraged.

rule: Sheets are numbered in sequence from 1 with no gaps; a single-sheet drawing is sheet 1.
note: same rule as TB-010.
quote: For multiple-sheet drawings, the sheets are numbered in sequence starting with 1.

rule: The total number of sheets is entered on sheet 1 only; later sheets show only their own sheet number.
note: Hanford convention. Conflicts with PARI's 'Sheet x of y' on every sheet (TB-010); do not enforce.
quote: Enter the total number of sheets on sheet 1 only.

rule: The Drawn By field gives the drafter's initials and surname (not a placeholder or login ID).
note: adds detail to TB-005. TB-005 checks the field is filled; this adds a format. Needs PARI's naming format (names, initials or employee codes).
quote: The initials and surname of the drafter are printed in the Drawn By box (see Figure 3).

rule: The drafting standard the drawing was made to is stated on the drawing.
note: same rule as LY-06. Presence of a standard reference (e.g. ISO 8015 or ASME Y14.5) is text-layer checkable; which one is the open ISO-vs-ASME question.
quote: The drafting standard used to develop the drawing shall be listed in the “REFERENCES” section of the drawing (see Figure 6).

rule: Documents the maker needs (specifications, vendor information) are listed with their document number and title.
note: adds detail to NM-03. Hanford has a REFERENCES block; PARI would cite standards and specs in the notes. Needs PARI's referencing practice.
quote: The reference document number is entered in the REF NUMBER field. The reference document title is entered in the TITLE field and may be abbreviated.

rule: The 'next used on' field gives the drawing number of the next higher assembly, or 'END ITEM' for a top-level drawing.
note: Only if PARI's template has a used-on field. Checking that the parent number is right needs PDM or assembly data.
quote: If the drawing is the top drawing, the words “END ITEM” are entered.

rule: Drawings affected by a design change are listed and cross-referenced both ways (new to existing and existing to new).
note: same rule as RV-04. Hanford DRAWING TRACEABILITY LIST block; needs other drawings.
quote: All existing drawings affected by a new design or modification need cross-referencing to the new drawings, and vice versa, to provide two-way traceability.

rule: Every reference to a general note in the drawing field (e.g. 'SEE GENERAL NOTE 5' or a flag-note number) points to a note that exists.
note: Generalises RQ-003 from the heat-treatment field to all note references. Text-layer check: parse 'NOTE n' references and the numbered notes list. A dangling reference leaves the shop without the requirement.
quote: a "flag note" or notation (for example, "SEE GENERAL NOTE 5") is placed in the body of the drawing near the affected area.

rule: A general note marked with a flag symbol in the notes list is flagged at least once in the drawing field, and every flag number in the field matches a flagged note.
note: Needs the flag triangle (vector geometry) around the note number; the number-to-note match itself is text-layer work. NM-07 is deferred.
quote: A flag note symbol is also placed in the general notes to indicate that a general note is flagged in the body of the drawing.

rule: On a multi-sheet drawing the general notes start on sheet 1 (preferred location: above the title block).
note: The 'above the title block' location is a layout preference; PARI's template sets the notes area.
quote: On multiple-sheet drawings, general notes start on sheet 1, but may continue on subsequent sheets, as necessary.

rule: Flag-note symbols are sized 0.38 in by 0.75 in as shown in Figure 8.
note: Inch-only figure (about 10 x 19 mm).
quote: If a flag note symbol is used, it is sized and configured as shown in Figure 8.

rule: A space about 75 mm high above the title block is kept for additional title-block information and stamps.
note: Hanford sheet layout (Figure 1).
quote: A space approximately 75 mm (3") high above the Title Block is reserved on the drawing for recording additional Title Block information

rule: Drawing originals are not changed by hand; the CAD master is corrected, re-plotted and re-approved.
note: CAD and records rule; related in spirit to DM-09 and LY-08 (content driven by the model).
quote: Manual modification of drawing originals is not permitted.

rule: Each revision after the initial release has approval initials or signatures in its revision-block entry.
note: adds detail to RV-001. At PARI submission the current revision's approval may be blank (TB-016); apply to earlier revision rows only.
quote: Revision 1 and higher approval signatures or initials are placed in the revision block.

rule: Each revision entry quotes the complete number of the change document that authorised it (e.g. 'REVISED PER ECN-1234').
note: same rule as RV-003. §3.12.6 (p31): 'REVISED PER [change document number]'. Hanford document types (FMP, DCN, ECR) map to PARI's ECN.
quote: When a drawing is revised, the complete authorizing change document number is placed in the revision description block (e.g. FMP, DCN, ECR, etc.).

rule: The revision description also records changes made beyond the authorising change document (e.g. 'added new sheet 3', 'moved detail X').
note: adds detail to RV-001. Verifying it needs the previous revision.
quote: A statement describing variances from the authorizing change document is added in the revision description block to document the changes.

rule: On a multi-sheet drawing, each sheet's revision is advanced only when that sheet changes, so each sheet's title-block revision must match that sheet's own revision block.
note: adds detail to TB-004. Hanford revises per sheet (added sheets are released as revision 0, §3.12.10). Many companies revise the whole drawing, so all sheets share one revision. PARI's convention decides which consistency check applies.
quote: Revision numbers are advanced only on the sheet or sheets being affected by the change.

rule: Revisions are listed in sequence in the revision block, and the latest one is the revision shown in the title block.
note: same rule as RV-007. Same paragraph: 'The latest revision number is shown in the Title Block' (TB-004). 'Each revision is released before another is made' is process, not checkable.
quote: Each new revision is listed in numerical sequence.

rule: On CAD-revised drawings, earlier approval signatures may be replaced by a 'SEE REVISION n' reference in the approval block.
note: Hanford practice. If PARI ever does this, TB-005 and TB-016 must accept 'SEE REV n' as a filled field.
quote: Reference to see the applicable revision is placed in the approval block (e.g., See Revision 0, or See Revision 5).

rule: A drawing that replaces another carries a 'SUPERSEDES DWG [number] REV [number]' note near the title block, giving both the drawing number and its revision.
source_document: HNF-64101 Rev 00 Preparation Standards for Engineering Drawings (Hanford, US DOE, 2020)
note: Runs only when a supersedes note exists. The old drawing's 'SUPERSEDED BY' note is outside v1's single-drawing view. PARI may handle supersession in PDM instead.
quote: On the New Drawing a note stating, "SUPERSEDES DWG [number] REV. [number]," is placed near the Title Block in 6 mm (.24") high lettering.

rule: Any change to a released drawing, including its title, is made through a new revision.
note: same rule as RV-10. Needs the previous revision.
quote: Changes in the title of an approved drawing are done through a revision.

rule: A drawing carrying controlled information is marked with its control designation (e.g. a confidentiality or export-control marking).
note: same rule as TB-018. DOE classification levels and the ADC review are not applicable; the general idea is PARI's ownership/confidentiality note.
quote: mark the drawing to reflect the security classification level and category or other required controls

rule: Units in notes are written as SI symbols in their correct form and case (mm, g, Pa, mm², L for litres), not spelled out or in non-standard forms.
note: PARI writes unit symbols in capitals in its all-capitals notes ('CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2 MM' on 88 of 1,175 client sheets); lower-case SI symbols would fire on those. Case matters (MM, KG are wrong). Reconcile with the all-capitals lettering candidate, which HNF exempts for unit symbols (§3.10.5). Litre symbol is upper-case L (§3.15.2, p35).
quote: Metric designations (e.g., mm) are considered symbols and are used to the fullest extent possible.

rule: Dimensions are hard metric (chosen in mm), not soft conversions of inch values.
source_document: HNF-64101 Rev 00 Preparation Standards for Engineering Drawings (Hanford, US DOE, 2020)
note: Our heuristic, not the book's: flag values that are exact conversions of common inch fractions (multiples of 1.5875 mm such as 6.35, 12.7, 19.05, 25.4) given to 2+ decimals. Warn only: imperial interfaces (US bought-out parts) can be legitimate.
quote: Soft metric measurements and conversions are to be avoided.

rule: Linear dimensions are in millimetres.
note: same rule as TB-009.
quote: Linear dimensions on engineering drawings shall be shown in millimeters, except on large site plans and civil drawings.

rule: Numbers do not use a comma as a thousands separator; values of five or more digits are grouped in threes with a space (1 500 000), and four-digit values are not split (5000).
source_document: HNF-64101 Rev 00 Preparation Standards for Engineering Drawings (Hanford, US DOE, 2020)
note: A comma read as a thousands separator versus a decimal comma can change a value 1000-fold. ISO allows a decimal comma and PARI's French notes may use one, so skip drawings whose decimal marker is a comma. The parser must not split a space-grouped number into two values.
quote: Commas are not used in metric system numbers. Spaces are used in place of commas to separate digits into groups of three (e.g., 1 500 000 mm).

rule: In notes, a space separates a number from its unit symbol (25 mm), and the number and unit are not split across lines.
note: Applies to notes and text; dimension values normally carry no unit. HNF states no exceptions (SI writes ° and % without a space; that exception is ours).
quote: A space always separates the numeric value from the measurement unit, but the number and the unit are never separated between the lines of text.

rule: Dimension values and unit symbols are in upright (not italic) lettering.
note: Italic/oblique style is in the PDF font name. ISO 3098 permits sloped lettering, so PARI's template font decides whether this applies.
quote: Metric dimensions and unit symbols are always in upright type (i.e., vertical lettering), even when the surrounding text is in italics.

rule: Dual dimensioning is avoided; where used, a general note explains the secondary values, they are placed the same way throughout, and each equals the primary value converted (1 in = 25.4 mm) and rounded so converted limits stay within the original limits.
source_document: HNF-64101 Rev 00 Preparation Standards for Engineering Drawings (Hanford, US DOE, 2020)
supporting_reference: D&T tutorial slides Unit of measure (p7-8); NASA GSFC-X-673-64-1F 10.2.2.2b-d (p104)
note: NASA GSFC 10.2.2.2c (p103) gives the rounding table (NASA-118 in the mapping). Only relevant if PARI shows inch values for US customers.
quote: A general note shall be added to the drawing stating the inch/pound dimensions shown in parentheses are equivalent to the metric dimensions they follow.

rule: A metric drawing carries the word METRIC (6 mm bold) directly above the title block.
note: adds detail to TB-009. ASME-style marking. PARI likely states units in the title block ('ALL DIMENSIONS IN mm'), which already satisfies TB-009.
quote: Drawings delineated in the metric system shall have the word “METRIC” placed directly above the Title Block in 6 mm bold gothic lettering

rule: The projection method is shown by the projection symbol together with the words naming it (HNF: 'THIRD ANGLE PROJECTION') next to the title block.
note: same rule as TB-07. HNF mandates third angle; PARI's projection angle is open. The words are text-layer checkable, and the symbol geometry (Figure 11, p36: concentric circles left of the frustum = third angle) could be compared with them.
quote: On metric drawings, the international projection symbol and the words "THIRD ANGLE PROJECTION" is placed directly above the metric notation.

rule: Thread and other trade-size designations keep their native form and are never converted (no '6.35 mm-20' for 1/4-20, no '.236-20' for an M6 thread).
note: adds detail to MC-005. Code check: a thread callout must parse as a standard designation (ISO metric M.., UNC/UNF, G/R/NPT pipe); decimal-mm inch threads or decimal-inch metric threads are flagged. Pipe sizes (DN 50 for 2 in) are piping, other_family.
quote: 1/4-20 thread loses its proper meaning if designated as 6.35 mm-20 thread; conversely, a 6 mm-20 thread loses its proper meaning if designated as a .236-20 thread

rule: Views, sections, dimensioning and tolerancing follow ANSI Y14.5M-1994.
note: adds detail to LY-06. SOURCE: NAAMS Global Standard Components, Assembly - Section A 'Design Drawing Standards and Tolerances' (sheets A-1 to A-39; index dated 05/29/15, sheets dated 1996-2015), (c) 1997 Auto/Steel Partnership, www.naamsstandards.org. Not one company's manual: NAAMS (North American Automotive Metric Standards) is the US automotive body-shop tooling standard (fixtures, transfers). PDF page N = sheet A-N. Sec. 8.1 says 'Y14.3M', apparently a typo for Y14.5M (Sec. 3.1). Conflict: PARI's ISO vs ASME choice is open, and its IS 2102 general tolerances suggest ISO/IS practice.
quote: Dimensioning and tolerancing practices shall be as defined and illustrated in ANSI Specification #Y14.3M - 1994.

rule: Orthographic views are drawn in third-angle projection.
note: adds detail to TB-07. PARI's projection angle is still open (Indian SP 46 practice is usually first angle). The book names the angle; TB-07 (symbol matches layout) is deferred.
quote: All drawings should be drafted using third angle projection on orthographic views.

rule: Section and auxiliary views are drawn perpendicular to their cutting or viewing plane, whether they sit on the same sheet or another one.
note: View-orientation check against the cutting-plane line; needs view-geometry analysis. Related to VW-02.
quote: When sections or views are projected on the same or on other sheets, they shall be projected and drawn perpendicular to the cutting or viewing plane.

rule: A section or view placed on a different sheet from its cutting or viewing plane has direction arrows on the cutting line and cross-reference notes on both the view and the cutting plane.
note: adds detail to VW-003. Multi-sheet PDFs: a view label with no matching cutting line on its own sheet must carry a sheet reference, and the cutting line must point to that sheet. Extends VW-003 (labels match cutting lines) across sheets.
quote: When sections or views are projected onto other sheets, directional arrows shall be shown and cross referencing notes added onto the respective view.

rule: Stock made to inch sizes (plate, tube, angle, channel) is called out with inch cross-section dimensions and a metric cut length.
note: Inch-stock rule; PARI drawings are metric. Repeated in the unit BOM instructions on p27.
quote: the cross section dimensions should be called out in U.S. customary units and the cut length in metric.

rule: Transfer equipment is dimensioned in metric, and travel distances also carry inch set-up dimensions for plant interfaces.
note: Tooling-system layouts, not single parts.
quote: Transfers within a tooling system shall have their construction dimensioned in metrics.

rule: Threads and fasteners are hard metric (ISO M sizes); inch threads such as UNC/UNF are not used, except pipe threads and existing inch commercial items.
note: adds detail to MC-005. Sec. 6.1 is a recommendation; Sec. 2.1 defines hard metric (not converted from inch). Exceptions come from Sec. 13.2-13.4 (p3). Text-layer regex for inch thread designations.
quote: It is recommended that all tool builders and suppliers use only hard metric fasteners.

rule: A metric thread callout with no pitch means coarse pitch; a fine thread states its pitch, and a stated pitch should equal the standard coarse pitch unless a fine thread is intended.
note: adds detail to MX-004. Coarse pitches are taken from the hole-chart label on p5 (M5 x 0.8 to M20 x 2.5). Check: report a stated non-coarse pitch as info (confirm fine thread intended); flag a pitch not valid for the diameter.
quote: All metric threads are assumed to be coarse unless otherwise specified.

rule: Tapped holes use the preferred sizes M5, M6, M8, M10, M12, M16 or M20, with M8 as the preferred minimum except where a commercial item has predetermined mounting holes.
note: adds detail to MC-005. Body-shop tooling preference. On general automation parts it would flag many small fasteners; only useful if PARI adopts a preferred tap list. The exception needs to know what the hole mounts (LLM).
quote: The preferred minimum screw size is M8, except for the attachment of commercial and standard items that have predetermined mounting holes.

rule: Kit fasteners, pivot shafts, bushings, bearings, cylinders and strokes, gears and racks (inch pitch) and pipe threads stay on their existing standards; energy, torque and power units are unchanged.
note: NAAMS inch-to-metric transition policy; not a drawing check.
quote: Pivot shaft diameters, bushing & bearing sizes, cylinders and stroke of cylinders etc., shall remain to existing standards.

rule: Decimal numbers below 1 are written with a leading zero (0.5, not .5).
source_document: NAAMS Global Standard Components, Section A: Design Drawing Standards and Tolerances (Auto/Steel Partnership, 2015)
supporting_reference: D&T tutorial slides Terminology / Standard Practices- Placement (figures) (p11, 25)
note: Applies to dimension and tolerance values in the text layer. ISO 129-1 and ASME metric practice agree, so no convention conflict.
quote: A zero before the decimal point shall be used for a number less than 1.0 (Example 0.5).

rule: The drawing and detail-view scales are full size where possible, otherwise a preferred scale: 1:2, 1:5, 1:10, 1:20 or 1:50 reduced, 2:1, 5:1, 10:1, 20:1 or 50:1 enlarged.
source_document: NAAMS Global Standard Components, Section A: Design Drawing Standards and Tolerances (Auto/Steel Partnership, 2015)
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Standard sheet sizes and scales, IS 696-1960 (pdf 67L, book 128); HNF-64101 3.11.7 (p26)
note: Matches the ISO 5455 preferred series, so no conflict (ISO also allows 1:100 and coarser; Sec. 9.4 leaves system-layout scales to the plant). Check title-block and detail-view scales (see TB-006, VW-008).
quote: The recommended reduced scale for fixture designs are 1:2, 1:5, 1:10, 1:20 and 1:50.

rule: Text is at least 2 mm high on 11 x 17 in sheets and 3 mm on other sheets; notes and descriptions are at least 5 mm; view, section and callout labels are at least 7 mm.
note: adds detail to LY-02. The PDF text layer gives font size, so this could move to v1. NAAMS values are far larger than ISO 3098 practice (2.5-3.5 mm), and 11 x 17 is a US sheet; PARI would need its own values.
quote: All text height shall be 2 mm minimum on 11 x 17 CAD drawings and 3 mm minimum on all other drawings.

rule: On fixture drawings, one body line in each direction is shown, related to the zero datum line and identified in a 25 mm balloon; auxiliary work lines are boxed with their origin and angle, and dimensions from a work line show their origin.
note: Automotive car-line coordinates on fixture layouts.
quote: On fixture drawings, only one body line is required in each direction provided its relationship to the zero datum line is shown.

rule: Dimensions are not taken to hidden lines.
note: same rule as MX-10. Published source for MX-10.
quote: Dimensions should be shown in true views and should not be taken from hidden lines.

rule: Features are dimensioned in a view that shows them in true size and shape.
note: same rule as VW-14. Published source for VW-14; related to DM-08.
quote: Dimensions should be shown in true views and should not be taken from hidden lines.

rule: Dimensions are placed outside the part outline wherever possible.
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70R, book 135); Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 71R, book 137)
note: Needs the part outline separated from dimension geometry. Soft rule ('wherever possible').
quote: Dimensions should be located outside the outline of the detail wherever possible.

rule: On assembly drawings, screw and dowel sizes are written along the fastener centre line in its side view.
note: Assembly drawings only.
quote: Screw and dowel sizes shall be written along the center-line of the fastener in its side view on assembly drawings.

rule: Metric commercial (bought-out) components are used where available and approved by the customer.
note: Purchasing/assembly matter; related to BM-16.
quote: Metric commercial components are preferred when available and approved by customer.

rule: Machined surfaces, pivot centre lines, hole patterns, fabrication dimensions and mounting surfaces are set on 5 mm increments where possible.
note: A code check could report location dimensions off a 5 mm grid. Only meaningful if PARI adopts the convention; noisy on general parts.
quote: Machined surfaces, pivot centerlines, hole patterns, fab dimensions and NC block mounting surfaces should be set up in 5 mm increments whenever possible.

rule: On unit (assembly) drawings, each detailed item has a 20 mm split balloon with the item number above and its detail sheet number below; purchased and standard items show only the item number; mirror details reuse the number marked SHN. and OPP.
note: Assembly balloons; related to BM-12.
quote: All items that are detailed shall be identified with a 20 mm diameter split balloon with the item number of the detail in the top half

rule: Dimensions and notes read from the bottom of the sheet (unidirectional) unless otherwise specified.
note: ASME uses unidirectional text; ISO 129-1 also allows aligned text read from the right, so this depends on the open ISO vs ASME question. Text rotation is in the text layer, so it is easy in v1 once decided.
quote: all dimensions and notes should be placed on the drawing so that they may be viewed from the bottom of the sheet.

rule: A dimension whose value does not match the drawn geometry at the view scale is underlined as not to scale; out-of-scale dimensions are otherwise avoided.
source_document: NAAMS Global Standard Components, Section A: Design Drawing Standards and Tolerances (Auto/Steel Partnership, 2015)
supporting_reference: D&T tutorial slides Standard Practices- Out-of-Scale Dimensions (p35, 76); NASA GSFC-X-673-64-1F 3.4d; 9.3.2 (p45)
note: Compare the value with dimension-line length divided by the view scale (vectors). ISO 129-1 uses the same underline. An unmarked mismatch is also a 2D sign of an overridden value (DM-09, phase2_3d). The book gives no comparison tolerance; one must be chosen. Severity major for that reason.
quote: when a dimension cannot be made to scale (as a result of a drawing revision), then the dimension should be underlined.

rule: When a long part is drawn broken to fit the sheet, the full dimension across the break is still given.
note: same rule as VW-13. VW-13 is phase2_3d for true-length checking; the 2D part (a dimension spans the break) needs break-line recognition.
quote: When details must be shown broken due to sheet size restrictions, the dimension for the missing section shall be written.

rule: Each revision entry describes the change completely enough to restore the previous version, for example by stating the old value.
note: adds detail to RV-001. The BOM instructions (p13, p31) say to note what the item 'was' before the revision.
quote: brief and accurate, but complete to the extent that the drawing could be reverted back to its original form.

rule: The same change letter is used on every sheet and related document (assembly, BOM) affected by a change.
note: adds detail to RV-04. Needs related documents. Unit BOM Sec. 25 adds that a change letter is used only once per unit.
quote: A change letter used when recording a change should continue to be used on all of the affected sheets (assembly, B.O.M., etc.) pertaining to that change.

rule: Every revision in the change column is marked on the drawing next to the changed item by its upper-case letter in a small (6 mm) balloon.
note: v1 can find letter-in-circle markers and match them to the revision table; it cannot tell whether every changed item is marked (RV-02). The first issue has no markers. PARI may use triangles; don't enforce 6 mm.
quote: A change letter (upper case) should be enclosed in a 6 mm diameter balloon. ... placed near the revision on the affected sheet.

rule: Change letters are listed in a vertical row in the change column, and each change balloon is repeated outside the border at the title-block end.
note: NAAMS template convention.
quote: A change letter and balloon should also be placed at the bottom and end of the sheet (title block end) outside the border

rule: Stock lists or bills of material are not placed on layout drawings.
note: Layout drawings only.
quote: Stock lists or bills of material should not be shown on layout drawings.

rule: On weldments, fabrication (fab zero-line) dimensions start from the same edges as the machining datum dimensions.
source_document: NAAMS Global Standard Components, Section A: Design Drawing Standards and Tolerances (Auto/Steel Partnership, 2015)
note: Keeps weld set-up and later machining on one origin. Related to WF-03 and MX-014. The LLM must tell fabrication dimensions from machining ones; PARI's separate IS 2102 classes may help.
quote: Fab “O” line dimensions should always start from the same edges as the machining datum line start dimensions.

rule: On weldments, the primary fabrication datums (X, Y, Z) are set on the primary member, usually the largest or the base footprint, and all member set-up dimensions run from them.
note: adds detail to MD-11. Weldment version of DT-14 (locating dimensions start from datums).
quote: All fab setup dimensions for sub-details should be dimensioned from the two primary Fab “O” lines.

rule: A weldment member that needs its own cut dimensions gets a secondary fabrication datum labelled with that member's item letter; auxiliary machining datum lines are numbered.
note: Labelling convention; PARI's weldment dimensioning scheme is not confirmed.
quote: When sub-details require “CUT” dimensions, secondary Fab “O” lines should be established for that particular sub detail.

rule: Holes are through unless the callout states a depth: when THRU is omitted the drawing carries the general note 'ALL HOLES THRU EXCEPT AS NOTED', and a blind hole states its depth in the hole callout.
note: adds detail to MX-003. Construction holes may also run to a cross hole (Sec. 21.2). MX-003 and DM-06 expect depth or THRU on every callout; accept the general note as the exception. PARI's convention is unknown.
quote: All tapped, dowel and clearance holes on details are assumed to be through; it will no longer be specified on a drawing that the hole is “THRU”.

rule: Counterbore depths are left off only for standard counterbores; a non-standard counterbore is dimensioned and noted 'AS SHOWN'.
note: adds detail to MX-003. Relies on a NAAMS standard counterbore table that is not in this section. PARI would need its own standard counterbore sizes before depth could be omitted.
quote: Depths for counterbored holes shall not be specified unless they are non-standard, in which case “AS SHOWN” should be noted on the drawing.

rule: A detail drawing with three or more hole sizes tabulates its holes in a hole chart giving a letter code, size and quantity for each tap, clearance and dowel size.
note: adds detail to MP-009. The trigger (3 or more sizes) is the concrete detail. Letter codes (AM, BM ... WM) are NAAMS-specific.
quote: On detail drawings with 3 or more hole sizes, holes shall be tabulated using the label shown.

rule: Clearance holes for metric screws use the standard sizes: M5 5.5, M6 6.6, M8 9.0, M10 11.0, M12 13.5, M16 17.5 and M20 22.0 mm.
note: adds detail to MC-005. Table on p5; screw-to-hole pairing follows the chart rows. Values equal the ISO 273 medium series. Needs the hole's screw size from the callout, hole table or vision summary. Assumption: a hole near but not equal to a table value is a likely error.
quote: CLEARANCE HOLES HM-5.5 JM-6.6 KM-9.0 LM-11.0 MM-13.5 NM-17.5 PM-22.0

rule: Dowel holes carry a fit class showing whether the dowel is a press fit or a slip fit, not just a nominal diameter.
note: same rule as TL-002. Published source for TL-002 (locating holes). Find dowel holes from 'DOWEL' text, the hole chart or fit codes.
quote: AFTER DOWEL SIZE, “H6” INDICATES PRESS FIT AND “F7” INDICATES SLIP FIT

rule: Dowel holes use H6 for a press fit and F7 for a slip fit, with m6 dowels in sizes 6, 8, 10, 12, 16 or 20 mm.
note: adds detail to TL-013. Tables on p5 (dowel sizes) and p6 (fits). H6/m6 is a transition fit; many ISO shops use H7 for dowel holes, so PARI's own fits would replace these.
quote: DOWEL HOLE TOLERANCES FOR PRESS FIT USE H6 ... FOR SLIP FIT USE F7 ... DOWEL TOLERANCE m6

rule: Slot callouts need not state CENT., TYP. or the end radius; centred, full-radius slot ends are assumed.
note: adds detail to NM-001. An exception for MX-08 (missing radius): don't flag full-radius slot ends.
quote: For slots, callouts for “CENT.”, “TYP.”, and “RADIUS” or “R” are assumed, and are no longer required.

rule: Every detail drawing is dimensioned from datum (zero) lines.
note: adds detail to MP-012. NAAMS zero-line (baseline/ordinate) practice, also behind Sec. 20 and the 'non accumulative' tolerance on p6. MP-012 marks the origin only when ordinate dimensioning is used; this makes it mandatory.
quote: All detail drawings should be datum lined.

rule: Raw stock sizes are not dimensioned on the detail drawing, except that one side is dimensioned when the stock section is nearly square.
note: adds detail to MF-003. Conflicts with MF-003 and MX-015 (stock size or thickness given): NAAMS puts stock sizes in the unit BOM. The near-square exception fixes orientation. Needs PARI's convention.
quote: No stock sizes shall be dimensioned on the drawing except that, when a stock size is close to being square, one side should be dimensioned.

rule: Stock sizes are listed on the bill of materials (for non-detailed items only per Sec. 22.4; for every detail per Unit B.O.M. Sec. 16).
note: Internal contradiction: p27 (1997) says 'The stock sizes of each detail must be listed'; p5 (2015) is newer.
quote: Stock sizes should not be noted on Bills of Material unless the item is ND (non-detailed item).

rule: On detail sheets, detail identification balloons are 20 mm and sub-detail (weldment member) balloons 7 mm in diameter.
note: NAAMS template style; v1 could measure circle diameters, but PARI's balloon style is unknown.
quote: Detail identification balloons (detail sheet) shall be 20 mm diameter and sub-detail balloons 7 mm diameter.

rule: Construction or tooling-ball studs use the recommended 6 mm stud diameter.
note: Specific to automotive checking fixtures.
quote: The recommended construction or tooling ball stud diameter is 6 mm.

rule: Untoleranced dimensions take their tolerance from the tolerance block by number of decimal places: 1 place machining +/-0.3, 1 place fabrication +/-1.5, 2 places +/-0.08 between machined surfaces (tighter for dowels and screw holes).
note: adds detail to TB-008. Table on p6. This decimal-place scheme conflicts with PARI's IS 2102 size-range classes. Under it, the decimal count sets the tolerance, so LY-005 would become a tolerance check.
quote: EXCEPT AS NOTED TOLERANCES SHALL BE: 1 PLACE MACHINING ±0.3 1 PLACE FABRICATION ±1.5 2 PLACE ±0.08 BETWEEN MACHINED SURFACES

rule: On weldments, the general tolerance note gives separate values for machined and fabricated (as-welded) dimensions.
note: adds detail to TB-008. Agrees with PARI's separate IS 2102 machining and fabrication classes. Check: drawings with weld symbols name both classes in the general tolerance note.
quote: 1 PLACE MACHINING ±0.3 1 PLACE FABRICATION ±1.5

rule: Dowel and screw-hole locations are held to +/-0.03 between dowels in one plane and from a dowel to its heel (locating) surface, +/-0.10 between dowels in different planes, and +/-0.13 to screw holes, non-accumulative.
note: adds detail to TL-002. Under IS 2102 general tolerances, dowel spacing would get about +/-0.1 to 0.2, too loose for doweling. Check that dowel-to-dowel and dowel-to-heel dimensions carry an explicit tolerance or position control within these values. 'Non accumulative' means measured from a common datum, not chained. PARI may set its own numbers.
quote: ±0.03 BETWEEN DOWELS IN THE SAME PLANE ±0.10 BETWEEN DOWELS IN DIFFERENT PLANES ±0.13 TO SCREW HOLES, NON ACCUMULATIVE

rule: Unless specified otherwise, finished surfaces have a maximum roughness set by the decimal places of their dimensions: 1 place 6 um, 2 places 3 um, 3 places 1.6 um.
note: adds detail to TL-016. Table on p6; values are evidently Ra 6.3 / 3.2 / 1.6. The decimal link doesn't carry over to IS 2102, but the pairs could seed an LLM cross-check for a tight tolerance on a rough surface.
quote: MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE ROUGHNESS OF ALL: 1 PLACE FINISH DIMENSIONS TO BE 6 MICRONS 2 PLACE FINISH DIMENSIONS TO BE 3 MICRONS 3 PLACE FINISH DIMENSIONS TO BE 1.6 MICRONS

rule: Surfaces used as machining datums (zero lines) are machined, unless they are cold-drawn or cold-rolled stock surfaces.
note: adds detail to TL-007. The symbol is NAAMS's zero-line (datum line) mark, which the text layer renders as 'O'. LLM check: datum faces carry a machining or roughness symbol, or the stock is cold finished.
quote: ALL MACHINING [zero-line symbol] SURFACES MUST BE FINISHED EXCEPT FOR COLD DRAWN OR COLD ROLLED SURFACES.

rule: U.S. customary tolerance block: 2 places +/-0.01 machining, +/-0.06 fabrication, 3 places +/-0.003 between machined surfaces, with inch dowel-hole limits.
note: Inch only.
quote: 2 PLACE MACHINING ±0.01 2 PLACE FABRICATION ±0.06

rule: Installation torques for metric screws follow the separate Fastener Installation and Torquing Procedure (NAAMS F-2.3).
note: No torque table in this book; related to BM-07.
quote: This page has been discontinued. Please refer to the Fastener Installation and Torquing Procedure, page F-2.3.

rule: Each BOM sheet shows its page number, page 1 shows the total ('1 of n'), and the header fields (description, customer, program, design and build source) are filled on sheet 1.
note: Repeated for each BOM type (p11, p16, p21, p26). Adding a sheet means revising sheet 1. Related to TB-010.
quote: List the page number on each page and the total number of system B.O.M. pages on page #1 only.

rule: Every BOM item has the same name as the title of its detail drawing, and the BOM shows the detail's current revision level.
note: Cross-document check: needs the BOM and the detail drawings.
quote: A name is to be given to every item listed and it should be the same name as on the detail drawing.

rule: Material for made details is specified by its standard material code (NAAMS: SAE number) and its supply condition, hot-rolled (HRS) or cold-rolled (CRS).
note: adds detail to MF-01. NAAMS puts this in the unit BOM, not on the detail. SAE codes differ from PARI's IS/EN grades (see WPE-001). The supply condition is the new detail; it ties to the p6 note that cold-finished surfaces need no machining.
quote: List the specific material type for make details. Use the S.A.E. material code number and specify if it is H.R.S. or C.R.S. finish.

rule: Unit BOMs list commercial items first, then customer standard items, then made items; each line has a source code (make, purchase, customer-furnished, rework, NC), quantities for one shown and one opposite unit, and an X in the service column for wear items.
note: BOM content; source legend on p32, service column on p31.
quote: List all detail components as shown on the layout drawings in the following order: commercial items, customer standard items, and make items last.

rule: Every change to a released BOM is recorded in its revision column with date, letter, description, the previous ('was') value and initials; removed lines are struck through with a single line, not erased.
note: If a carried-over item is removed from all units, all affected BOMs and layouts must be revised (p18, p23, p31).
quote: Lines removed or canceled from a B.O.M. must be crossed out with a single line and not erased.

rule: BOM levels (system, line, tool, unit), who fills each, release order, fabrication-only versus final release, long-lead items and -R/-L tool-number suffixes follow the NAAMS process.
note: NAAMS organisation and release process; BOM templates on p36-39.
quote: A “Final Release” on any detail or component constitutes authorization to construct or order those items.

rule: Reference dimensions are enclosed in parentheses and are for information only, not used to make the part.
note: same rule as DM-010. SOURCE: untitled-author slide deck 'Dimensioning and Tolerancing' (94 slides). No author, institution, course or date appears on any slide and the PDF metadata is empty (PDFium export). Figures and the cross-reference 'Figure 14.50' (p58) look adapted from a Bertoline et al. McGraw-Hill graphics-communication textbook (inferred, not stated). Convention: ASME (p40 'Current ASME Y 14.5-1994 standards', p73 'ASME/ANSI symbols'), third-angle view layouts (p21, p22, p46, p48), mostly inch units with metric examples. THIS ROW: matches DM-010; p10 figure shows reference dimension as (2.00).
quote: Reference dimension is the numerical value enclosed in parentheses provided for information only and is not used in the fabrication of the part.

rule: Basic dimensions are shown enclosed in a rectangle (box) and carry no tolerance of their own.
source_document: Dimensioning and Tolerancing tutorial slides (author not stated; ASME Y14.5-1994)
note: p10 figure labels a boxed .50 as 'Basic dimension'; boxed basics also on p85 and p90. Check: a boxed value must not carry +/- or limits. Complements MX-011 (missing basic dimension), which checks presence, not format.
quote: Basic dimension is the numerical value defining the theoretically exact size of a feature.

rule: Every dimension has a tolerance, either applied directly or covered by a general tolerance note.
note: same rule as MX-012. Also TL-01 (merged).
quote: Every dimension must have an associated tolerance, and that tolerance must be clearly shown on the drawing.

rule: A general tolerance note covers all dimensions that are not individually toleranced.
note: same rule as TB-008. Figure-based (the +/- sign renders as '+' in the slide). PARI uses IS 2102 classes in place of a single +/- value.
quote: ALL FORMATS +.05 UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED

rule: Metric dimension values below 1 are written with a leading zero (0.95, not .95).
note: Figure-based: inch values omit the leading zero (.125, .375), millimetre values keep it (0.95). Only the metric half applies to PARI. Text-layer regex check.
quote: Decimal dimensioning ... .125 ... Millimeter dimensioning ... 0.95

rule: Dimension text height meets the minimum: 3 mm on metric drawings (.125 in on inch drawings).
note: adds detail to LY-02. Conflict: LY-02's example is 2.5 mm on A3/A4 (ISO-style); this ASME-based source shows 3 mm. PARI's value to confirm. Font size is in the PDF text layer, so code-checkable once the value is fixed.
quote: TEXT HEIGHT 3mm ... TEXT HEIGHT .125"

rule: Diameter dimensions are preceded by the diameter symbol (Ø) and radius dimensions by R; no 'DIA' suffix or 'D' forms.
source_document: Dimensioning and Tolerancing tutorial slides (author not stated; ASME Y14.5-1994)
source_section: Terminology; Detail Dimensions - Holes; Dimension Guidelines (p17, 37, 52)
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70R, book 135)
note: Only dimension values and callouts. 'DIA' in revision descriptions (44 client sheets, e.g. '2-M6 TAP & DIA.6.6 ADDED') is not a finding.
quote: Diameters must be dimensioned with the diameter symbol preceding the numerical value.

rule: Hole callouts use the standard symbols (counterbore, spotface, countersink, depth, square) before the value rather than words (C'BORE, SP FACE, C'SINK, DP), and one drawing does not mix the two styles.
note: adds detail to LY-11. p40 contrasts ASME Y14.5-1994 symbols with 'THRU C'BORE', 'X 1.00 DP', 'THRU C'SINK 82'. p76 marks counterbore, countersink and depth as 'ISO-proposed', so ISO-convention drawings may use words. The 'don't mix styles' part is v1-checkable now.
quote: Diameters, radii, squares, counterbores, spotfaces, countersinks, and depth should be specified with the appropriate symbol preceding the numerical value.

rule: Leaders for diameter and radius dimensions are radial (they point at the centre of the circle or arc).
note: p37 figure shows a correct (radial) and incorrect (non-radial) leader to Ø40. Needs leader direction vs arc-centre geometry.
quote: Leader lines for diameters and radii should be radial lines.

rule: No feature is dimensioned twice or in more than one way (no over-dimensioning).
note: same rule as DM-002. p20: 'Dimensions should not be excessive, either through duplication or dimensioning a feature more than one way.'
quote: Avoid over-dimensioning a part. Double dimensioning of a feature is not permitted.

rule: Every feature has the size dimensions needed to make it.
note: same rule as MX-001. Also DM-01 (merged).
quote: The basic criterion is, "What information is necessary to make the object?"

rule: Every feature has location dimensions, e.g. from an edge of the part to the centre of a hole.
note: same rule as MX-002.
quote: Location dimension might be length from the edge of the object to the center of the drilled hole.

rule: Overall width, height and depth of the part are given.
note: same rule as MX-005. Figure-based and weak: p22 shows width, height and depth as the size dimensions of a part. Also DM-05 (merged).
quote: Size dimensions ... Depth ... Width ... Height

rule: Every angle other than 90 degrees is dimensioned (by an angle or by two coordinates); lines drawn at right angles are taken as 90 degrees unless stated.
note: adds detail to MX-009. Exception for MX-009: don't flag right angles. p48 'Alternate Method' shows an incline given by 30 degrees in place of a second length.
quote: Unless otherwise specified, angles shown on drawings are assumed to be 90 degrees.

rule: In rectangular-coordinate (baseline/datum) dimensioning, all dimensions in each direction start from one baseline, and the origin (0,0) is clearly identified.
note: same rule as MP-012. p24 figure labels 'Origin (0,0)' and datum surfaces for X and Y.
quote: a base line (or datum line) is established for each coordinate direction, and all dimensions specified with respect to these baselines.

rule: In tabular dimensioning, every hole tagged with a letter has its size given in the hole table.
note: same rule as MP-009. Figure-based: holes tagged A/B on an ordinate-dimensioned plate, sizes in a symbol table.
quote: Symbol A B / Hole diameter 20 10

rule: The first dimension line is at least 10 mm from the part outline and parallel dimension lines are at least 6 mm apart (on the plotted sheet).
note: adds detail to VW-06. Adds numeric limits to VW-06 (legible, no overlap). Computable from vector dimension-line positions; deferred per the drafting-quality class.
quote: The minimum distance from the object to the first dimension is 10mm (3/8 inch). The minimum spacing between dimensions is 6mm (1/4 inch).

rule: Extension lines start with a visible gap from the feature and extend about 1 mm past the last dimension line.
supporting_reference: Westermann Tables Dimensioning (pdf 70L, book 134)
note: Internal conflict in the source: p26 text says about 1 mm overshoot, the p26 figure says 'Approximately 2mm'.
quote: A visible gap shall be placed between the end of extension lines and the feature to which they refer.

rule: When space permits, the dimension value and arrows sit between the extension lines; otherwise they go outside.
quote: When space permits, dimensions and arrows are placed between the extension lines.

rule: Related dimensions are grouped and aligned in a common line, not scattered around the view.
note: Figure (A) Yes: chain dimensions in one row with the overall; (B) No: same dimensions scattered.
quote: Dimensions should be grouped for uniform appearance as shown.

rule: Where several parallel dimensions are stacked, their values are staggered so they don't crowd each other.
note: adds detail to VW-06. Specific technique under VW-06 (legibility).
quote: Where there are several parallel dimensions, the values should be staggered.

rule: Extension lines do not cross dimension lines and avoid crossing other extension lines; they are not broken where they cross object or extension lines, only at arrowheads.
note: Line-crossing geometry analysis.
quote: Extension lines should not cross dimension lines, and should avoid crossing other extension lines whenever possible.

rule: Holes and other centred features are located to their centre lines (the centre line serves as the extension line), not to their edges.
source_document: Dimensioning and Tolerancing tutorial slides (author not stated; ASME Y14.5-1994)
source_section: Standard Practices- Extension lines; Basic Concepts (p21, 31)
note: Vision summary of what each dimension refers to can flag hole locations taken to an edge. Related VW-10 (centre lines present).
quote: When the location of the center of a feature is being dimensioned, the center line of the feature is used as an extension line.

rule: A point located only by extension lines (e.g. a theoretical corner on a rounded bend) has the extension lines passing through it.
note: same rule as MX-24. p31 figure (B): bent bar dimensioned 48 and 41 to theoretical intersections. Related DM-13 / MX-24.
quote: When a point is being located by extension lines only, the extensions lines must pass through the point.

rule: A limited length or area that gets extra treatment (knurl, polish, hardening, label area) is bounded by a chain line parallel to the surface and dimensioned for size and location.
note: adds detail to WPM-003. Generalises WPM-003 (hardened area shown) to any partial treatment; also relevant to MF-006 masking and MX-019 knurl. p32 figures: DIAMOND KNURL, POLISH, hatched area 'Place label in this area' located by 10/40/20/40.
quote: the extent of the limits may be shown by a chain line. The chain line is drawn parallel to the surface being defined.

rule: All dimension and note text reads from the bottom of the sheet (unidirectional), not aligned with the dimension line.
note: Slide labels unidirectional 'Current standard' and aligned 'Old standard' (ASME view); ISO 129-1 still allows aligned text. Text-layer rotation makes it code-checkable; a v1-safe variant is 'one orientation method used throughout'.
quote: All dimension and note text must be oriented to be read from the bottom of the drawing (relative to the drawing format).

rule: Dimensions are placed outside the view outline where practical; inside only when leaders would be too long or clarity improves.
note: p34 figure (A) No: dimensions inside the view; (B) Yes: outside.
quote: Placing dimensions within the boundaries of a view should be avoided whenever practicable.

rule: A dimension whose value does not match the drawn geometry at the stated scale (not to scale) has its value underlined.
note: Check: measured dimension-line length / sheet or view scale vs value; a mismatch without underline suggests a manually overridden value (see DM-09, phase2_3d). Source gives no mismatch tolerance. Exclude broken views (VW-13). p76 lists the underline as 'Dimension not to scale'.
quote: If it is necessary to include a dimension which is out of scale, the out of scale dimension text must be underlined.

rule: Repeated features carry the count as 'nX' plus a space before the dimension (e.g. 4X Ø.375), and the count equals the number of features drawn.
note: adds detail to MX-006. Parser must not confuse the count 'nX' with the chamfer form '2 X 45°' (p38). ISO drawings write '4×'. Count vs features drawn needs the vision summary.
quote: The number of repetitions, followed by the symbol X and a space precedes the dimension text.

rule: Chamfers are fully specified: a 45° chamfer by length X 45° or length X length, other chamfers by length and angle, internal chamfers by diameter and angle.
note: adds detail to NM-001. Figure-based: external 30° chamfer given by 2 and 30°; internal chamfers by Ø40 and 90° (included) or 45°. A chamfer with a single value is incomplete.
quote: 2 X 45° or 2 X 2 ... Internal Chamfers

rule: Slots are fully dimensioned: width, plus overall length or centre-to-centre length (or a 'W X L' note), plus the end radii.
note: adds detail to MX-001. Three accepted methods shown. In every example the end radius is half the width (R5 for width 10), so a code cross-check R = W/2 is possible, though the slide does not state it as a rule.
quote: Slotted holes ... 40 ... 10 ... 2 X R5 ... 10 X 40

rule: Keyseats and keyways give the key width and a depth measured from the bottom of the keyseat (or top of the keyway) to the opposite side of the shaft or bore.
note: adds detail to MC-007. Figure-based: .500 on a Ø.625 shaft is taken from keyseat bottom across to the far side, so it can be measured directly. Keyways in hubs may sit on non-round parts.

rule: Diameters of concentric turned features are dimensioned in the longitudinal (rectangular) view, not as circles in the end view.
note: adds detail to MX-10. Figure-based: all six diameters are staggered on the sectioned side view; the circular view carries none.
quote: Concentric circles ... Ø 150 Ø 100 Ø 75 Ø 50 Ø 40 Ø 20

rule: Arcs are dimensioned by radius (R) in the view where they appear as arcs, and arc centres not on other features are located.
note: same rule as MP-11. Figure-based: centres marked with crosses; the R46 centre is located by the 80 and 95 dimensions.

rule: Each feature is dimensioned in the view that shows its shape most clearly (its contour), e.g. a radius where it appears as an arc.
note: same rule as MX-10. p46 figure: correct vs incorrect contour dimensioning of a notch and a radius.
quote: Dimensions should be placed in the view which most clearly describes the feature being dimensioned.

rule: Dimensions are not taken to hidden lines where avoidable.
note: same rule as MX-10. Dashed (hidden) lines are in the vector layer, so an extension-line-endpoint-on-dashed-line test is possible later.
quote: Dimensioning to hidden lines should be avoided whenever possible. Hidden lines are less clear than visible lines.

rule: Inch screw threads are called out as size-pitch, series and class, with A for external and B for internal threads (e.g. .50-13 UNC-2A / -2B).
note: Inch-only. The metric analogue (6H internal / 6g external) is not shown in the slides; thread completeness is MX-004.

rule: Grooves are dimensioned by width plus depth or groove diameter, with the bottom radius where the groove is radiused.
note: adds detail to MX-001. Figure-based: groove given as width + diameter, or width X depth (depth symbol).

rule: Material made to gauges or code numbers (sheet, wire) has its thickness stated as a numerical value, not only a gauge number.
note: adds detail to MF-003. p45 shows an inch sheet-metal gauge table: gauge numbers mean different thicknesses per gauge system. Also MX-015.
quote: Dimensions for materials typically manufactured to gages or code numbers shall be specified by numerical values.

rule: Dimensions do not specify the manufacturing method (drill, ream, punch, bore) unless only that method is acceptable.
note: same rule as NM-12. NM-12 is deferred; a text-layer keyword scan could raise it as a warning in v1. PARI may legitimately write REAM (dowel holes), so warning only.
quote: Manufacturing methods should not be specified as part of the dimension unless no other method of manufacturing is acceptable.

rule: Blind, counterbored and countersunk holes state their depth in the callout along with the diameter.
note: same rule as MX-003.
quote: The depth of blind, counterbored, or countersunk holes may be specified in a note along with the diameter.

rule: A hole callout with no depth and no THRU is read as a through hole; flag it only when the hole is blind or the views don't show it passing through.
note: adds detail to MX-003. Exception to MX-003 to cut false positives: under the slide's ASME-1994 convention 'THRU' is omitted when the section shows the hole through. PARI's habit to confirm.
quote: Current ASME Y 14.5-1994 standards ... Through hole ... Ø .50 ... Previous standards ... Ø .50 THRU

rule: Counterbore and spotface callouts give the diameter (and depth for a counterbore); countersink callouts give the diameter and included angle.
note: adds detail to MX-003. Figure-based. Also relates to MX-003 (depth) and MX-009 (angle).

rule: In limit dimensioning the upper limit is placed above the lower limit.
note: adds detail to RQ-002. Figure-based (also 2.510 over 2.490 on p10). Text-layer y-positions of stacked values give the order.
quote: 3.53 ... 3.49 ... (A) Direct limits

rule: In plus/minus tolerancing the plus deviation is placed above the minus deviation, and a zero deviation is written as a plain 0 (e.g. 22 0/-0.3, 12 +0.1/0).
note: adds detail to RQ-002. Figure-based; unilateral and bilateral metric examples.

rule: Angles are given in decimal degrees or in degrees-minutes-seconds with unit symbols, and an angle's tolerance uses the same format (e.g. 25.6° 0/-0.2°, 25°15' ±0°5').
quote: Angular dimensions are shown either in decimal degrees or in degrees, minutes, and seconds.

rule: The drawing states its unit of measure (otherwise a US reader assumes inches).
note: same rule as TB-009. Relevant to PARI drawings going to US customers.
quote: On a drawing used in American industry, all dimensions are in inches, unless otherwise stated.

rule: Where dual dimensioning is used, the secondary values are placed the same way throughout (bracket or position method) and equal the primary value converted (1 in = 25.4 mm).
note: p8 shows the position method (127 over 5.00) and bracket method (5.00 [127], 1.00 [25.4]). 25.4 comes from the examples. Pure text-layer arithmetic.
quote: Occasionally, a company will used dual dimensioning, that is, both metric and English measurements on a drawing.

rule: Metric tolerance classes use an uppercase letter for internal features (holes, e.g. H8) and a lowercase letter for external features (shafts, e.g. f7); in a fit callout the hole class comes first (H8/f7).
note: adds detail to TL-013. A wrong-case class (e.g. h7 on a bore) reverses the deviation direction. Internal/external comes from the vision summary or geometry.
quote: HOLE 40 H8 ... SHAFT 40 f7 ... FIT 40 H8/f7

rule: Where limits are shown with a tolerance class (40H8 (40.039/40.000) or the reverse), the limits equal the ISO 286 values for that size and class.
note: adds detail to TL-013. Three accepted designation methods. Quick arithmetic sub-check: an H hole's lower limit and an h shaft's upper limit equal the basic size (p69-72 hole/shaft basis).

rule: Fit classes used are among the standard hole-basis (H11/c11, H9/d9, H8/f7, H7/g6, H7/h6, H7/k6, H7/n6, H7/p6, H7/s6, H7/u6) or shaft-basis (C11/h11 ... U7/h6) fits; others are noted for review.
note: adds detail to TL-013. The slide does not call these 'preferred'; the table matches the ANSI B4.2 preferred metric fits. On single-part drawings check each class half (e.g. H7, g6) against the list. Footnote: H7/p6 is a transition fit for basic sizes 0-3 mm.
quote: ISO Symbol ... Hole Basis ... Shaft Basis ... Description

rule: The fit chosen suits the stated function: running, sliding, locational, or drive/shrink.
source_document: Dimensioning and Tolerancing tutorial slides (author not stated; ASME Y14.5-1994)
note: Uses the p71 descriptions (loose running H11/c11 ... force fit H7/u6). Only when the function is evident from notes or the feature (bearing seat, dowel hole). Related TL-002 / TL-003.
quote: Sliding fit not intended to run freely but to move and turn freely and locate accurately

rule: When both mating limits are known, the allowance (smallest hole minus largest shaft) gives the intended fit type: positive for clearance, negative for interference.
note: adds detail to TL-013. Needs the mating part's limits; v1 only if a combined fit (e.g. Ø40 H8/f7 with both limits) is on the drawing.
quote: Allowance always equals smallest hole minus largest shaft

rule: Inch fits use the ANSI classes RC, LC, LT, LN and FN.
note: Inch-only.
quote: Standard Precision Fit; English Units

rule: Form tolerances (straightness, flatness, circularity, cylindricity) do not reference a datum.
note: adds detail to TL-005. Figure-based: every form frame in the slides carries only a symbol and value (e.g. flatness .002, circularity .010); orientation frames carry a datum. Mirror of MD-003.
quote: All Points on Surface Must Be between the 2 Planes

rule: A diameter symbol in a tolerance frame is used only for an axis control applied to a cylindrical feature of size (frame attached to its size dimension); flatness, circularity, cylindricity and surface-element straightness never take one.
note: adds detail to TL-005. p79: line-element straightness has no Ø and a leader to the surface; axis straightness has Ø and sits under the Ø.500 size dimension. p84: axis perpendicularity likewise. Text-layer check plus frame-to-dimension attachment from vectors.
quote: Ø.002 (always) True Axis of Shaft, 3-Dimensional Twist ... .002 Tolerance Zone Size

rule: MMC and LMC modifiers appear only on tolerances of features of size (not on flatness, circularity, cylindricity or runout), and not on position tolerances of tapped holes or threaded inserts.
source_document: Dimensioning and Tolerancing tutorial slides (author not stated; ASME Y14.5-1994)
supporting_reference: related rule TL-10; NASA GSFC-X-673-64-1F App. A (j) (p120)
note: TL-10 (deferred) is about deliberate use; this validity part is text-checkable. Examples: axis straightness Ø.002Ⓜ, position Ø.005Ⓜ, datum feature at MMC (p91).
quote: MMC Modified ... Ø.002 (at least) Plus any Bonus Tolerance

rule: Under the envelope principle (perfect form at MMC), a form tolerance on a feature of size is tighter than its size tolerance, or it adds no control.
note: Derived from the figure (ASME Rule #1 envelope), not stated as a rule; example Ø.500/.495 with circularity .002. ISO 8015 defaults to independency unless the envelope symbol or a note applies, so this depends on PARI's standard (LY-06).
quote: Perfect Circle, Cannot Exceed MMC Size

rule: Orientation, location and runout tolerances (parallelism, perpendicularity, angularity, concentricity, runout, position) reference a datum.
note: same rule as MD-003. Every orientation/location frame in the slides names datum A (and B, C for position).
quote: .002 Between Perfect Planes (parallel to datum)

rule: A feature controlled by angularity has its angle given as a basic (boxed) dimension, not a toleranced angle.
note: adds detail to MX-011. Figure-based: the 60° and 30° angles are boxed. A toleranced angle plus angularity is a double control.

rule: Position-toleranced features are located by basic dimensions from the datums named in the frame.
note: same rule as MX-011. Also TL-09 (merged). p90: 3X Ø.500±.004 located by boxed 1.00/2.00/1.25/.75 from datums B and C.
quote: Cylinders or holes located at exact basic dimensions from -A-

rule: Position tolerances on fastener clearance holes are consistent with the hole-to-fastener clearance (floating-fastener case), or split between the two parts when the fastener is fixed in one.
note: The slides give no formula (the usual one, T = H - F floating and T = (H - F)/2 fixed, is not in the source). Needs fastener size / mating part. Related TL-12.
quote: Floating fastener tolerancing is used to confirm that loose bolts, screws or other fasteners have the standard clearance in their holes.

rule: The datum reference frame follows the part's functional priorities.
note: same rule as MD-09. Also DT-05 / DT-06 (merged). Needs assembly function.
quote: Identify the datum reference frame based on functional priorities.

rule: The drawing states which drafting standard it follows, because ASME and ISO symbol sets differ.
note: same rule as LY-06. p76 marks all-around and arc length 'ISO-none' and counterbore, countersink and depth 'ISO-proposed'.
quote: GDT is a method of defining parts based on how they function, using standard ASME/ANSI symbols.

rule: The sheet is one of the IS 696-1960 trimmed sizes A0 to A5 (A0 841 × 1189, A1 594 × 841, A2 420 × 594, A3 297 × 420, A4 210 × 297, A5 148 × 210 mm), in either orientation.
note: adds detail to TB-015. The PDF page size gives the sheet size directly; allow a small rounding tolerance. TB-015 checks the company template; this adds the size list.

rule: Small sheets are used upright (vertical); either orientation is allowed, but vertical use is preferred for the smaller sizes.
note: The book does not define 'smaller sizes'. PARI's FR-DES-006-01 template fixes the orientation, so confirm with PARI before checking.
quote: The sheets may be used vertically or horizontally. With the smaller sizes the vertical usage of sheets is preferred.

rule: The drawing and view scales come from the IS 696-1960 series: full size 1:1; reduced 1:2.5, 1:5, 1:10, 1:20, 1:50, 1:100, 1:200; enlarged 2:1, 5:1, 10:1.
note: adds detail to DSM-012. Partly CONFLICTS with DSM-012: the book lists 1:2.5 (not 1:2), has no 20:1 or 50:1, and adds 1:100 and 1:200. 1:2 is common on CAD drawings; ask PARI which series applies. The page prints '1 50' with the colon missing.

rule: The scale of the drawing is stated in its place in the title block.
note: same rule as TB-006. TB-006 also compares the stated scale with the main view.
quote: The scale of the drawing should be indicated in the appropriate place in the title block.

rule: When views on one sheet are drawn to different scales, the scale of each such view is shown under that view.
note: same rule as VW-008. 'Detail' is used in the older sense of a drawn part or view. Placement under the view matches the usual Solid Edge view label.
quote: If more than one detail drawn to different scales occurs on a sheet, the corresponding scale should be shown under each relevant detail.

rule: The title block sits in the bottom right-hand corner of the sheet.
note: adds detail to TB-015. Template-level check; the text positions of the title-block fields give its location.
quote: The title block should be placed at the bottom right hand corner of the sheet where it is readily seen when the prints are folded.

rule: The title block gives the drawing title, the name of the organisation or firm, the drawing number, the scale and the date of the drawing.
note: same rule as TB-001. Also covered by TB-003 (title), TB-005 (date) and TB-006 (scale); the firm name is the only field no existing rule names.
quote: presents details like title of drawing, name of organisation or firm, drawing number, scale, date of drawing, etc. in a definite manner.

rule: The title block is 150 × 50 mm on A0 to A3 sheets, may take the full sheet width on A4, and is 185 × 42 mm (horizontal) or 123 × 50 mm (vertical) on A5.
note: PARI's template FR-DES-006-01 defines its own title block, which probably differs. Worth checking once on the template, not on every drawing.
quote: Size for A0, A1, A2, A3 IS 150×50 mm. For A4 it may occupy the full width of the sheet. For A5 horizontal 185×42 mm and vertical 123×50 mm.

rule: The title block has a Tolerance field, and it is filled in.
note: same rule as TB-008. The IS 696-1960 title block has a Tolerance box under Scale, presumably for the general tolerance; see WST-077 for the IS 2102 class.
quote: Drg, Dm, Chd, Trd, Comp ... Scale ... Tolerance ... Additional Information ... Name of Firm ... HEADING ... Approved ... DRG NO

rule: The title block shows the projection-method symbol.
note: same rule as TB-07. TB-07 is deferred because it also matches the symbol against the view layout. Presence alone is a vector check (two concentric circles and a trapezoid near the title block). Which angle applies is open with PARI (see WST-016).
quote: Name of Firm ... [projection symbol: concentric circles and truncated cone] ... Approved ... DRG NO

rule: Each sign-off row of the title block (drawn, checked, traced, compared, approved) has a name column and a date column, and the drawn row is filled with both.
note: same rule as TB-005. Traced and Compared are hand-drafting steps with no CAD equivalent. TB-016 wants Checked and Approved blank at submission, so only the Drawn row has to be filled.
quote: Date ... Name ... Drg, Dm, Chd, Trd, Comp ... Dm, Chd, Trd, Comp, Appd

rule: The revision record gives a revision number, date, brief record of the change and dated initials for every revision.
note: same rule as RV-001. Shown in the parts-list title block; the columns match RV-001 (description, date, author).
quote: R.No. ... Date ... Brief Record ... Dated Initials

rule: A separate parts list gives, for every item, the part number, description, drawing or reference number, material, number off and any additional information.
note: Assembly/BOM content. It matters because PARI writes material '#' (see parts list) on 86% of sheets, but v1 cannot see the parts list. Its title block also has Part List No., Supplement and Drg. No.
quote: A typical form of separate material or parts list is shown here. Part No. ... Description ... Drawing No.or Ref. No. ... Material ... No. Off

rule: Each line type is used for its purpose: thick continuous for outlines, thin continuous for dimension, extension and hatching lines, medium short dashes for hidden lines, thin long-and-short chain for centre lines, a thick chain of one long and two short dashes for cutting planes, and freehand lines for short breaks.
note: same rule as LY-01. IS 696-1960 conventions: medium-weight hidden lines and the two-short-dash cutting-plane line look old; PARI's template decides. The break line is labelled Medium but its sample widths are the thick ones (1.00/0.80/0.6), and pdf 69L calls local breaks thick. The book prints Brake for Break.
quote: Hidden lines Short dashes closely and evenly spaced ... Cutting plane lines One long and two short dashes ... Brake lines for short brakes Free hand lines

rule: Line widths come from one IS 696-1960 group (thick 1.00, 0.80 or 0.60 mm with medium 0.50, 0.45 or 0.40 and thin 0.30, 0.25 or 0.20), keeping thick about three times and medium about twice the thin width, and one centre-line dash ratio between 6:1 and 4:1 is kept throughout the drawing.
note: adds detail to LY-01. Stroke widths are in the vector PDF, but the team defers line-weight checks. The text says thick may be 1.00, 0.84 or 0.60 mm while the table shows 0.80 (probably a misprint). PARI's Solid Edge template sets the real widths. On centre lines the table adds: In one drawing ratio selected must be maintained.
quote: Lines specified as thick should be three times as thick and lines specified as medium twice as thick than those specified as thin.

rule: The drawing uses third-angle projection, the standard method IS 696-1960 recommends, and shows the matching symbol.
note: IS 696-1960, in PARI's own reference book, recommends third-angle projection (book p129). The edition is old and PARI's projection angle is still open: ask PARI. CONFLICT with the brief's assumption that the book follows first-angle European practice: this page recommends third angle (it shows both). PARI's projection angle is still open; don't enforce until PARI confirms.
quote: The standard method of projection recommended in IS is the third angle projection.

rule: Views are placed as the projection method requires: in first angle the view from above goes below the front view and the view from the left goes on its right; in third angle the view from above goes above it and the view from the left on its left.
note: same rule as VW-02. Needs view identification and placement; the vision summary might support a warning later. The first-angle figure labels view 3 View from front, a misprint for view from left.
quote: Methods of projection and arrangements of views ... View from above ... View from below ... First angle projection ... Third angle projection

rule: Surface-finish triangles follow IS 3073-1967: one triangle means Ra 8 to 25 µm, two mean 1.6 to 8, three mean 0.025 to 1.6 and four mean below 0.025.
note: Old convention (triangles instead of Ra-valued symbols); PARI may or may not still use it. A check could flag more than four triangles, or an Ra value outside the band of its triangle count. Triangles are symbol-font or vector items; vision can't read them.
quote: surface roughness is by triangles and the same is suggested here ... 8 to 25 Ra µm ... 1.6 to 8 ... 0.025 to 1.6 ... < 0.025

rule: A surface roughness symbol carries its characteristics in fixed places around the symbol: roughness criterion, machining method, sampling length, machining allowance and direction of lay.
note: IS 3073-1967 symbol layout; PARI's symbol standard decides. The book doesn't say which fields are mandatory, so a check can only test placement of what is given. Needs symbol geometry.
quote: it is very essential to indicate a certain place for them in the symbol. Surface roughness criterion, Machining method, Sampling length, Machining allowance, Direction of lay

rule: Each roughness value lies within the range that the stated or implied manufacturing process can reach in the IS 3073-1967 table (e.g. turning and milling Ra 0.32 to 25 µm, drilling 1.6 to 20, reaming 0.4 to 3.2, surface and cylindrical grinding 0.063 to 5).
note: adds detail to TL-016. The process is usually not written; the check can take it from the feature type in the vision summary (e.g. a plain drilled hole) and warn. A value finer than the range implies an extra finishing operation. Ranges read from a bar chart whose header gives no unit; the section uses Ra µm.
quote: Surface roughness expected from manufacturing processes ... Turning and milling 0.32 ... 25 ... Drilling 1.6 ... 20 ... Reaming, broaching and hobbing 0.4 ... 3.2

rule: Prints larger than A4 are folded to 210 × 297 mm with the title block on top and visible.
note: Handling of paper prints, not drawing content; PARI issues PDFs.
quote: The title block must be on top and be placed properly so that it is visible. ... Fold to a height of 297 mm

rule: Lettering heights are taken from the series 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20 and 25 mm.
note: adds detail to LY-02. The PDF text layer gives font sizes, so this may be v1-checkable once font size is converted to capital height h; kept deferred to match LY-02. The book gives no minimum per sheet size.
quote: Sizes of letters height=2 2.5 3 4 5 6 8 10 12 16 20 25 mm

rule: Lettering keeps the IS proportions to the capital height h: lower-case letters 5/7 h, stroke width 1/7 h and line spacing 11/7 h, with inclined lettering at 75°.
note: Set by the CAD font rather than the drafter (see LY-03). The book shows inclined lettering; whether PARI uses upright or inclined text is its font choice.
quote: the height of lower-case letters=5/7 h, the width (line width)=1/7 h, the line to line distance=11/7 h. Angle of inclination=75°

rule: Section hatching is drawn in thin, evenly spaced lines at a clear angle, preferably 45° to the axis or main outline, with spacing in proportion to the size of the section; large areas may be hatched only in a band along the outline.
note: adds detail to VW-09. Hatch lines are vectors, so angle and spacing are measurable, but hatching checks are deferred with VW-09. The large-area exception is a separate panel on the same page.
quote: thin lines at a well defined angle, preferably 45° to the axis or the main outline of the section. Spacing ... should be in proportion to the hatched section.

rule: Hatching is interrupted where a dimension value or lettering sits inside a hatched area, so no hatch line crosses the text.
note: adds detail to ISO-029. ISO-029 already forbids lines crossing dimension values; this adds the hatching case. Needs text bounding boxes and hatch-line vectors.
quote: For figuring or lettering hatching may be interrupted.

rule: Adjacent parts cut in a section are hatched differently: two adjacent parts at 45° in opposite directions, and a third part at 30° or 60°.
note: adds detail to VW-09. Assemblies. On v1 single-part drawings VW-09 already asks for one pattern per part.
